jobs.description:
About Veeco

You probably don’t realize it, but what we do at Veeco touches the lives of every person, every day. It’s a bold statement, but it’s true. From the smartphones in our pockets that access the world’s collective knowledge, to the cloud-based services where all that information lives, to high-speed wireless communication and computing power needed to drive artificial intelligence, augmented and virtual reality, gaming and so much more, our technology is all around us.

We design, develop, manufacture, and service highly complex, cutting-edge machines used by our customers to create the essential devices that drive the digital age, connect the world, and improve the human experience. Along with the world’s leading technology companies, many of which are household names, we help solve their most difficult material science challenges, enabling technologies for a more connected, sustainable, and convenient world.

We’re looking for material difference-makers to join our growing team. Interested? Learn more at www.veeco.com/careers .

Overview

Bring Next-Generation Semiconductor Equipment to Life

As an Engineering Program Manager, New Product Introduction (NPI), you will lead cross-functional programs that transform customer and market needs into technically sound, production-ready products. You will work at the intersection of Marketing, Technology, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Technical Support, and Field Service, providing the program leadership needed to move sophisticated wafer processing equipment from product definition and engineering development through validation, design release, and production readiness.

Operating with significant independence within the Engineering PMO, you will own the integrated program plan and drive alignment across multidisciplinary engineering and business teams. You will establish milestones, coordinate dependencies, monitor engineering maturity and BOM/ECO readiness, manage schedules, cost, risk, and product lifecycle deliverables, and drive timely resolution of issues that could impact program commitments.

Why this opportunity stands out:
This role puts you at the center of complex engineering innovation, where your program leadership directly influences how new technologies progress from market and product requirements into manufacturable, supportable products. You will collaborate across the product lifecycle, gain broad exposure to technical and business functions, and have meaningful influence over program execution, priorities, trade-offs, and critical decisions.

This is more than a project tracking role. You will bring together people, technology, and execution to solve complex problems and turn engineering activity into measurable program outcomes. You will anticipate risks, facilitate critical decisions, remove barriers to execution, and establish the cross-functional operating rhythm needed to successfully transition products from development and validation into a repeatable, manufacturable, and supportable production environment.

Responsibilities

NPI Program Leadership and Product Definition

Lead assigned NPI programs from Marketing identification of customer and market needs through product requirements, engineering development and validation, design release, production readiness, and formal project closeout.
Partner with Marketing, Technology, Systems, and Engineering teams to establish program scope, objectives, requirements, deliverables, milestones, assumptions, dependencies, and success criteria.
Own the integrated program plan and operating cadence, including task planning, milestone reviews, action tracking, status reporting, decision management, and cross-functional follow-through.

Engineering Execution and Design Maturity

Coordinate multidisciplinary Mechanical, Electrical, Systems, Software, Controls, and related engineering activities to maintain alignment between technical workstreams and overall program commitments.
Track engineering maturity and release readiness, including drawings, specifications, bills of material (BOMs), Engineering Change Orders (ECOs), validation activities, open technical issues, and Product Life Cycle (PLC) deliverables.
Drive structured issue resolution, trade-off discussions, and escalation of technical or execution risks that could affect requirements, qualification, schedule, cost, manufacturability, or product readiness.

Production Readiness and Cross-Functional Integration

Partner with Operations and Supply Chain to drive production-readiness activities such as material readiness, sourcing dependencies, manufacturing documentation, tooling or fixture needs, build planning, and transition of released product structures into ERP/MRP systems.
Coordinate with Technical Support and Field Service to address serviceability, installation, support, documentation, and product-introduction needs required for a successful release and field transition.
Facilitate readiness reviews and closure of critical gaps to confirm cross-functional deliverables are sufficiently mature to support pilot builds, release, ramp, and downstream product support.

Program Controls, Risk, Cost, and Communication

Manage program schedules, critical-path activities, risks, issues, dependencies, resource constraints, and recovery actions; proactively communicate impacts and escalate decisions when needed.
Monitor product cost targets, costed BOM maturity, engineering project budgets, and key cost drivers; coordinate corrective actions with Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations when performance is off plan.
Provide concise, data-driven program updates to Engineering PMO and cross-functional leadership, clearly communicating status, accomplishments, risks, trade-offs, decisions required, and next steps.

Continuous Improvement and PMO Support

Lead or support Continuous Improvement Projects (CIP) and engineering initiatives that improve product performance, reliability, cost, manufacturability, serviceability, or execution effectiveness.
Contribute to consistent Engineering PMO practices, including planning standards, program reviews, risk management, lessons learned, and reusable NPI processes and tools.
Collaborate with and support other Program Managers while independently leading assigned programs, workstreams, or complex engineering projects appropriate to a Level III role.

Qualifications

Minimum

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
Minimum 5 years of experience managing complex engineering, product development, or NPI programs requiring coordination across multiple technical disciplines and business functions.

Preferred Qualifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent formal project management training.
Experience supporting semiconductor capital equipment, vacuum systems, wafer processing equipment, or similarly complex automated electro-mechanical products.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional NPI execution from product requirements and engineering validation through design release and production readiness.
Working knowledge of complex electro-mechanical systems incorporating robotics, vacuum pumps, motors, heaters, power supplies, instrumentation, PLC/control systems, and PC-based controls.
Ability to understand engineering drawings, system architecture, BOM structures, ECO/change-control processes, technical dependencies, verification and validation status, and product-readiness criteria.
Strong program-management capability across scope, schedule, milestones, resources, cost, risk, issue resolution, change management, and stakeholder communication.
Ability to analyze ambiguous, interdisciplinary problems, organize complex information, identify critical paths and trade-offs, and drive teams toward timely decisions and closure.
Experience coordinating product cost, costed BOM, lifecycle deliverables, and cross-functional readiness activities in a complex manufacturing environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, PowerPoint, and project planning/scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project; SAP or comparable ERP/MRP experience preferred.
Familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or SolidWorks and the ability to work effectively with engineering design data is preferred.
Excellent written, verbal, and executive-facing communication skills with the ability to influence without direct authority across technical and business functions.
Adaptable, organized, and results-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining ownership, urgency, and attention to detail.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Major Projects
jobs.description:
Spark Power Corp USA is seeking an experienced Program Manager, Major Projects
who will be accountable for the successful end-to-end delivery of large and complex programs and projects, spanning both high voltage and low voltage electrical infrastructure work. This role provides senior project leadership across the full project lifecycle – from initial scoping and estimating through engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout – for programs that may include multiple concurrent projects, sites, contractors, and internal delivery teams.

Our ideal Program Manager, Major Projects
candidate will be the single point of accountability for assigned programs, the Program Manager, Major Projects leads cross-functional and often cross-regional teams, manages client and stakeholder relationships at a senior level, and ensures that safety, quality, schedule, and financial targets are met or exceeded. This position blends the technical rigor of a traditional high voltage/low voltage Project Manager with the broader coordination, governance, and reporting responsibilities required to run programs at scale

What
will you do in this position?

Program & Project Leadership
Serve as the single point of accountability for the successful delivery of assigned major projects and programs, spanning high voltage and low voltage electrical scopes.
Lead project teams (internal staff, subcontractors, and vendors) through all phases of the project lifecycle: initiation, planning, execution, monitoring/control, and closeout.
Where a program includes multiple linked projects, provide overall program governance – coordinating scope, schedule, and resource interdependencies across individual project managers and workstreams.
Identify and pursue opportunities for account growth and follow-on work within existing client programs.

Team Leadership & Resource Management
Lead, mentor, and develop project managers, engineers, coordinators, and site supervisors assigned to the program, fostering a high-performance and safety-first culture.
Coordinate with resource/branch managers to secure the labour, equipment, and materials needed to meet project commitments.
Set clear expectations, provide regular performance feedback, and support the professional development of project team members.

Risk Management & Reporting
Identify, assess, and mitigate project and program risks (technical, commercial, safety, schedule) throughout the project lifecycle.
Maintain accurate project documentation, including status reports, risk registers, meeting minutes, and lessons-learned records.
Provide timely, accurate reporting to senior leadership on program health, financial performance, and key risks/issues.

Do you have the Spark
? Here’s what we’re looking for:

Bachelor's degree or diploma in Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, Engineering Technology, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience will be considered.
5+ years of progressive project/program management experience delivering electrical infrastructure projects, with direct experience in both high voltage (>800V) and low voltage systems.
Demonstrated success managing large-scale, multi-site, or multi-year programs, including projects with total installed value in the multi-million-dollar range.
Prior experience in substation construction, utility/industrial electrical projects, renewable energy (solar/wind/BESS), or comparable heavy electrical infrastructure work is strongly preferred.
Experience managing subcontractors, EPC-style delivery, and client-facing commercial relationships.
Professional Engineering designation (P.Eng. in Canada or PE in the U.S.), or active pursuit of licensure, is strongly preferred.
Candidates holding a Red Seal/journeyman certification as an Electrician or Powerline Technician, combined with equivalent field leadership and project delivery experience, are equally encouraged to apply and will be given strong consideration in lieu of a P.Eng./PE designation.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or working toward one, preferred.
Valid driver's license and ability to travel to project sites as required.
Additional relevant safety certifications (e.g., NFPA 70E, First Aid/CPR) are an asset.

Working Conditions

Combination of office-based work and regular travel to active project and client sites (estimated 25–50%, varying by program phase).
May require site visits to active construction, substation, or utility environments; adherence to all site-specific PPE and safety requirements is mandatory.
Occasional evening/weekend availability may be required to support critical project milestones, outages, or commissioning events.
Valid passport and ability to travel across Canada and/or the United States, as applicable to assigned programs

Diverse and exciting industrial, commercial and institutional projects and customer base
Growing company with consistent work
Continuous training and skills improvement
Career advancement opportunities
Competitive wages
Travel opportunities
Excellent benefit package (Medical, Dental, Vision, Extended Health, Disability)
401k with percentage company match

Great company culture!
….and much more

Power
?

Spark Power is the leading independent provider of end-to-end electrical services and operations and maintenance services to the industrial, utility, and renewable asset markets in North America. Job Title:
Surveillance Program Manager

Vacancies:
This posting is for (1) current vacancy

Location:
Vancouver, BC | Ottawa, ON | Calgary, AB | Halifax, NS | St John's, NL | Kelowna, BC| Prince George, BC | Montreal, QC | Québec, QC (Detailed office location information can be found by visiting this link: https://cancer.ca/en/contact-us)

Hybrid Work Model

6 ($72,000 - $82,000 CAD)

HELP SHAPE THE FUTURE OF CANCER CARE IN CANADA

The Canadian Cancer Society works tirelessly to save lives, improve lives and drive collective action against cancer. Together with patients, volunteers, donors and communities across the country, we raise funds to invest in transformative cancer research, we provide a caring support system for everyone affected by cancer and we advocate to governments to create a healthier future for all. It takes a society to take on cancer – and the Canadian Cancer Society is leading the way.

MAKING AN IMPACT

Reporting to the Director, Surveillance, the Surveillance Program Manager plays a critical role in leading the operational delivery, coordination and continuous improvement of the Canadian Cancer Society's surveillance and cancer statistics programs. The role is responsible for managing complex multi-partner initiatives, supporting national advisory committee and working group structures, overseeing the production and dissemination of flagship surveillance products, coordinating external vendor and partner relationships, and ensuring efficient program operations.

The Program Manager serves as a key point of contact for the Canadian Cancer Society’s national surveillance portfolio, including the Canadian Cancer Statistics program, implementation of the pan-Canadian Cancer Data Strategy and the Data Transformation grant program. The Program Manager works with key external collaborators including Statistics Canada, the Public Health Agency of Canada, the Canadian Partnership Against Cancer, provincial and territorial cancer registries, academic experts and volunteers, people with lived and living experience, as well as internal CCS teams to ensure high-quality surveillance products are delivered on time and with impact. The Program Manager provides enabling support to the Director, Surveillance, to expand key relationships with national and international collaborators and interest holders.

What You’ll Be Doing

Program Implementation and Management
Manage end-to-end implementation of multi-interest holder cancer surveillance and data programs and projects, including operational planning, coordination, monitoring and knowledge translation.
Develop and maintain integrated workplans, production schedules, risk logs, and reporting processes across Surveillance initiatives.
Manage the governance and operations of the Canadian Cancer Statistics Advisory Committee, including meeting planning, logistics, agendas, minutes, action-item tracking and committee communications, as well as the nomination process for members and chairs.
Coordinate monthly collaborator meetings, semi-annual senior collaborator meetings and strategic working groups, including methods, evaluation and special report subcommittees.
Lead production management for Canadian Cancer Statistics publications, special reports and knowledge translation products from planning through publication and evaluation.
Manage additional surveillance-related publication production workflows involving authors, reviewers, copyeditors, graphic designers, translators and publication vendors.
Support the Surveillance leadership in preparing for and executing follow-up actions from meetings, including development of communications, presentations, conference abstracts, reporting compilation, among others.
Lead the development and continuous improvement of project management processes, standard operating procedures, templates, and tools to support the Surveillance team and improve efficiency and quality.
Delegate coordination of administrative project deliverables to various Surveillance and CCS staff to deliver knowledge products and events.
Provide mentorship to Surveillance staff to build capacity and support career development.
Relationship Management and Interest-holder Engagement
Build and maintain strong working relationships with federal collaborators (Statistics Canada, the Public Health Agency of Canada), academic collaborators and advisors, provincial and territorial cancer registries, researchers, contractors, people with lived and living experience, and volunteer experts.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal teams (e.g., Fundraising; Communications; Digital Engagement; Digital Marketing and Solutions; Data Strategy, Analytics and Solutions; Advocacy and Health Policy; Research; Cancer Information; Cancer Prevention; Cancer Strategy and Innovation) to ensure alignment and collaboration to maximize impact and reach of Surveillance products.
Support relationship building with key international collaborators and interest holders, including, but not limited to, the International Agency for Research on Cancer, international and regional cancer registries, global health organizations (e.g., WHO), among others.
Manage communications and engagement activities leading up to publication releases, including webinars, briefings and pre-release meetings.
Lead the execution of launch activities, including strategic kick-off events and collaborative planning sessions that align internal and external interest-holders with CCS’s priorities.
Coordinate interest-holder outreach and dissemination activities for surveillance publications, reports and knowledge products.
Support preparation of briefing notes, presentations, reports, committee materials and executive updates for CCS leadership.
Financial and Administrative Management
Manage Surveillance program budgets, contracts, invoices, expense claims and vendor agreements.
Coordinate vendor procurement and relationships, including translation, graphic design, editing and digital platform providers, as required.
Monitor budget performance and support annual planning and forecasting activities.
Maintain Surveillance SharePoint resources, program records and documentation systems.
Coordinate administrative processes that support effective delivery of the Surveillance portfolio.
Coordinate updates to cancer.ca and related digital dissemination channels for Surveillance content.
Other
Foster a high-performance culture that leverages the unique talents and strengths of each member while encouraging their growth and development.
Champion CCS as a hero in the face of cancer.
Contribute to our culture of diversity, inclusion, belonging and equity (DIBE) by ensuring that all staff feel represented, valued, and heard across all aspects of their identity, including gender, age, religion, ethnicity, nationality, race, and sexuality.
Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Master's degree in Health Administration, Business Administration, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Sciences, or a related field.
Project Management Professional (PMP) designation or equivalent project/program management certification.
5+ years - extensive job-related experience in progressively more senior positions.
Knowledge translation, evaluation, or implementation science training considered an asset.
Experience managing complex multi-partner programs or initiatives with multiple deliverables and timelines.
Demonstrated experience developing strong partner relationships and working in collaborative environments involving governments, academic institutions, and non-profit organizations
Experience supporting committees, advisory groups or governance structures.
Experience coordinating publication, reporting and knowledge translation activities.
Experience with budget administration.
Extensive experience developing project plans, timelines, reports and operational processes
Strategic and systems thinking
Strong customer service, relationship building, communication and interpersonal skills
Excellent attention to detail and quality management
Ability to maintain the confidentiality of sensitive information
Excellent communication skills including the ability to write clearly and succinctly in a variety of styles; communicate with technical and non-technical audiences
Bilingualism (French/English) is highly preferred, with French being an asset due to the organization’s nationwide operations and the need for effective communication across various regions.
Others may apply
For roles based in Quebec, French is required. Knowledge of another language may be required depending on job responsibilities and business needs.

What You Can Expect From Us

CCS provides impactful opportunities to transform the lives of Canadians affected by cancer. We are devoted to creating an inclusive workplace that celebrates diverse experiences and skills, encouraging all qualified candidates to join us. Our inspiring culture is rooted in our core values and commitment to meaningful change:

COURAGEOUS UNITED CARING RIGOROUS

We offer a competitive salary, excellent benefits, including paid parental leave, family sick time, and health insurance—and a fulfilling work environment where your efforts make a meaningful impact daily.

COME AS YOU ARE

At CCS, we celebrate individuality and the strength of diversity. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace that empowers everyone. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including those from equity-deserving groups such as BIPOC, 2SLGBTQI+ communities, individuals with disabilities, veterans, and others who contribute to the richness of our organization. Together, we unite Canadians to shape the future of cancer care.

Overview:

Overview

The Enterprise Resilience Role helps strengthen the organization’s ability to anticipate, withstand, respond to, recover from, and adapt to cyber, technology, operational, and third-party disruptions. The role connects technical recoverability with business continuity and critical business service outcomes. It partners across Cyber Security, Information Technology, Disaster Recovery, Business Continuity, Emergency Management, business operations, and vendor management to establish consistent resilience requirements, validate recovery capabilities, track gaps, and drive measurable improvements.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can work across technical and business teams, bring structure to a developing enterprise program, and translate resilience risks into clear actions and decisions.

Key Responsibilities

Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Enterprise Resilience Program, including governance, standards, procedures, playbooks, reporting, and program documentation.
Help identify and maintain Critical Business Services and map the people, processes, technology, data, facilities, and third parties required to deliver them.
Partner with business and technology owners to define and validate impact tolerances, recovery time objectives, recovery point objectives, minimum service levels, and recovery priorities.
Plan, coordinate, and document resilience assessments, business impact analyses, tabletop exercises, disaster recovery tests, cyber recovery exercises, and simulations.
Track findings, risks, decisions, owners, due dates, and corrective actions through closure; identify recurring themes and escalate material gaps when needed.
Enhance backup and recovery capabilities, including Rubrik, Azure-native backups, SQL-native backups, and Veeam.
Improve ransomware-resilient recovery capabilities through immutable backups, clean-point validation, data-integrity checks, malware-aware recovery practices, and secure restoration workflows.
Help build and mature the isolated recovery environment, including automation of restoration testing and repeatable validation of recoverability.
Participate in disaster recovery exercises with infrastructure, application, security, and business teams to confirm that systems, data, integrations, and business processes can be restored and validated.
Coordinate cyber, business, and enterprise tabletop exercises to test decision-making, communications, downtime procedures, manual workarounds, escalation paths, and recovery actions.
Support containment, response, and recovery activities during disruptive events, including coordination across technical and business teams and documentation of key decisions.
Conduct after-action reviews and convert lessons learned into prioritized, assigned, and measurable improvements.
Assess third-party resilience capabilities supporting critical services, including continuity plans, recovery commitments, testing evidence, dependencies, concentration risks, and contingency options.
Develop dashboards, metrics, and executive-ready reporting for recovery readiness, testing coverage, unresolved risk, remediation progress, and resilience maturity.
Create clear technical and business documentation, standards, procedures, and repeatable processes that reduce manual effort and improve consistency.
Promote resilience awareness by helping stakeholders understand their roles before, during, and after a disruption.

Education

Bachelor's (Preferred)

Certification/Licensure

Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CBCP, CRISC, or Microsoft Azure certifications. (Preferred)

Experience

With a degree: Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in IT program/project management.
Five or more years of experience in enterprise resilience, cyber resilience, disaster recovery, business continuity, infrastructure, information security, risk management, or a related discipline.
Working knowledge of ransomware-resilient recovery, immutable storage, clean recovery, isolated recovery environments, and restoration validation.
Experience planning or supporting disaster recovery tests, tabletop exercises, incident response activities, or business continuity exercises.
Ability to analyze complex service dependencies and connect technical recovery capabilities to business and operational outcomes.
Experience documenting risks, control gaps, corrective actions, procedures, and evidence in a structured and auditable manner.
Strong project coordination and follow-through, including the ability to manage multiple workstreams, owners, dependencies, and deadlines.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical risk and recovery issues to both technical and business audiences.

Ability to remain organized and effective during high-pressure incidents and work constructively across teams where processes or ownership are still maturing.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in healthcare, another highly regulated industry, or a complex organization with critical 24/7 operations.
Knowledge of business impact analysis, critical business services, impact tolerances, crisis management, third-party resilience, and operational resilience practices.
Familiarity with cloud resilience patterns, particularly Microsoft Azure, including identity, data, application, infrastructure, and regional recovery considerations.
Experience creating resilience metrics, reporting, dashboards, maturity assessments, or executive presentations.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CBCP, CRISC, or Microsoft Azure certifications.
Enterprise resilience assessments that include technology, business operations, workforce, facilities, data, and critical third parties.

2 years of experience in asset disposition.

Experience developing and deploying security programs around confidential prototypes and unreleased products.

Preferred qualifications:

R2, CSDS (Certified Secure Destruction Specialist) or CPP (Certified Protection Professional).
Experience with "demanufacturing" processes—knowing exactly how to take apart a proprietary device to extract value without compromising secrets.
Deep understanding of and experience in loss prevention/asset protection, conducting security risk assessments, physical security systems and processes, investigations, and corrective action planning (CAPA), writing and implementing security standards, along with basic understanding of EHS work flows and waste control regulations.
Demonstrated high ethical standards with the ability to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately, with excellent judgment, discretion, and diplomacy.
Ability to travel domestically or internationally.

About The Job

We are seeking a Global Destruction Program Manager to design, implement, and oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of our most sensitive physical assets. This is not just a waste management role; it is a critical security function. You will be responsible for ensuring that prototypes, defective/decommissioned high-value components, proprietary pieces of hardware, devices, components and materials are rendered non-recoverable. You will lead a global network of certified vendors, ensuring that our intellectual property never leaks, ends up on the secondary market or in the hands of competitors.

From keeping Googlers safe and secure to managing disruptive events, the ability to anticipate, deter, detect, and act are the pillars of Google’s Global Security and Resilience Services (GSRS) team. As a member of GSRS you will help develop a culture where safety, security and resiliency are integrated into every facet of Google, including the creative process. You will help us continually identify, evaluate and monitor enterprise risks that could affect business activities and provide business leaders the information they need to make critical decisions. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams to create innovative strategies and develop programs that drive sustainable effectiveness.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $157000 - $227000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Develop and maintain global Secure Destruction SOPs aligned with security leadership, ensuring compliance with international trade, local laws, and data privacy regulations.
Source, manage, and physically audit global destruction, smelting, and recycling partners via unannounced site visits to guarantee compliance.
Classify critical Alphabet IP to define destruction standards, deploying RFID/GPS tracking to maintain end-to-end chain of custody through final certification.
Conduct risk assessments, threat benchmarking, and lead investigations into asset leaks, theft, or grey-market breaches alongside cross-functional stakeholders.
Leverage AI tools and program metrics to drive operational efficiency, scale secure workflows, and continuously modernize scrap destruction practices.

Permanent Exempt (PEX)
: Full Time position is excluded by the Charter from the competitive civil service examination process and shall serve at the discretion of the appointment officer. ✅ A resume and cover letter are required at the time of application.

About the Office of the City Administrator:

The Office of the City Administrator
includes 20+ agencies and over 1,000 dedicated staff who provide essential services to San Francisco residents and businesses and improve the administration of government.

Our Mission

The City Administrator’s Office is strongly committed to ensuring efficient and effective government services, increasing the City’s safety and resiliency, strengthening the local economy, supporting equity and inclusion, and optimizing the City’s capital planning and infrastructure.

Our Vision

We are committed to ensuring that the City's services are inclusive, efficient, equitable, and culturally competent for San Franciscans of all races, ethnic backgrounds, religions, and sexual orientations. This commitment requires comprehensive review and thorough analysis of existing practices and policies to remove barriers to real inclusion.

We are also committed to ensuring that the Department is a safe, equitable, and inclusive workplace for individuals of all races. This includes creating opportunities for hiring, promotion, retention, training, and development, for all employees, including but not limited to Black, Indigenous, and people of color (BIPOC).

To learn more about our departments, divisions, and programs, visit: https://sf.gov/departments/city-administrator

About the Government Operations Initiative:

The Government Operations Initiative (GovOps) brings together teams across the City Administrator’s Office, Controller’s Office, and Department of Human Resources to tackle complex operational challenges that cut across traditional departmental boundaries. Launched in 2022 with an initial focus on supporting the City’s recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic, GovOps focuses on improving the systems, policies, and processes that underpin City operations, with a focus on procurement and contracting, hiring, and financial operations.

GovOps teams combine project management, policy and process expertise, data analysis, and change management to develop and implement complex reforms. Our work requires understanding how City processes operate today, identifying where they create unnecessary burden or barriers, and partnering across departments to design and implement practical improvements.

The Procurement Reform Team

The Senior Project Manager will join the GovOps Procurement Reform team within the City Administrator’s Office. Our team leads citywide efforts to make procurement and contracting simpler, faster, more effective, and more accessible for both the City staff who use these processes and the suppliers who do business with the City.

Our portfolio spans policy and legislative reform, business process redesign, technology modernization, data and performance, and improvements to the supplier experience. We take on complex problems that often cross organizational and functional boundaries, working from initial problem definition and research through design, implementation, change management, and evaluation.

While our core team is small, our work is highly collaborative. We partner closely with the Office of Contract Administration (OCA), Contract Monitoring Division (CMD), Department of Technology (DT), Controller’s Office (CON), and contracting professionals and operational teams across City departments.

In our work, we strive to be dynamic and responsive to City staff and supplier needs, and we are guided by questions such as:

How can we make City processes simpler and more effective without losing the safeguards necessary for responsible stewardship of public resources?
How can we reduce barriers for small and local businesses, community-based organizations, and other suppliers seeking to do business with the City?
How do we design reforms that are ambitious enough to meaningfully improve government while also being practical, sustainable, and responsive to the people who will use them?

This role is an opportunity for someone who is motivated by convoluted but compelling challenges in governance, enjoys bringing order to ambiguity, and is interested in finding the right balance between incremental and transformational change. We are looking for someone who is committed to ensuring that public institutions serve communities equitably and sees themselves as a public-sector leader.

Job Description

The Senior Project Manager will lead the team’s technology, policy, systems, data, and performance portfolio, driving complex initiatives that improve how the City purchases goods and services and how suppliers do business with the City. The role will have a particular focus on leveraging emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, modernizing procurement systems, and strengthening the use of data and performance management to improve City operations. As one of two GovOps team leads, this position will lead high-priority, cross-departmental projects from strategy and design through implementation and continuous improvement. The Senior Project Manager will report to the Deputy Director of Operations and Procurement Reform in the Office of Contract Administration.

Examples of Important and Essential Duties:

Procurement Process & Policy Reform: Lead initiatives to improve City procurement and contracting processes, including business process redesign, policy and legislative changes, and exploration of emerging technologies such as AI. Identify pain points and opportunities for improvement, develop solutions, and lead implementation of reforms that reduce administrative burden while appropriately managing risk.
Technology Procurement Reform: Lead initiatives to make the City’s technology purchasing processes faster, clearer, and more effective. Projects may include streamlined pathways for lower-risk technology purchases, improvements to City contract templates and purchasing programs, and reforms to cybersecurity review and procurement processes.
Procurement Systems & Digital Tools: Lead the design and implementation of citywide applications, tools, and technology that improve procurement operations and the supplier experience. Translate business needs into system requirements and coordinate with technical teams and end users to develop solutions such as tools for searching contract documents, managing supplier compliance documentation, and improving access to procurement information.
eProcurement Implementation: Lead OCA’s planning and implementation of a new eProcurement system, including procurement and contracting, business requirements, system configuration, testing, data and process readiness, user onboarding, change management, and risk and issue resolution.
Team Leadership & Supervision: Supervise and develop staff responsible for data, performance, and systems work, including setting priorities, assigning and reviewing work, providing coaching and feedback, and supporting staff development. Provide strategic direction for the team’s portfolio.
Cross-Functional Project Leadership: Build and manage strong working relationships across OCA and with key City partners, including CMD, the Department of Technology, CON Systems, and other departments. Establish project governance, workplans, communications, decision-making structures, and performance measures to keep complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives moving forward.

Qualifications

Education:

Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and:

Experience:

Seven (7) years of full-time equivalent experience performing professional level analytical work. Qualifying professional-level analytical work includes analysis, development, administration, and reporting in major programs and functions of an organization in the areas of budgets, contracts, grants, policy, or other functional areas related to the duties of positions in the 182X Class series.

Substitution:
Possession of a graduate degree (Master's degree or higher) from an accredited college or university with major coursework in specialized subject matter areas such as public or business administration, management, business law, contract law, public policy, urban studies, economics, statistical analysis, finance, accounting or other fields of study closely related to the essential functions of positions in the Class series may be substituted for one (1) year of required experience.

Additional experience as described above may be substituted for the required degree on a year-for-year basis (up to a maximum of 2 years). Thirty (30) semester units or forty-five (45) quarter units equal one year.

One-year full-time employment is considered equivalent to 2000 hours (2000 hours of qualifying work experience is based on a 40 hour work week). Any overtime hours that you work above forty (40) hours per week are not included in the calculation to determine full-time employment.

jobs.title: Principal Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

Rocket Lab’s Space Systems division builds complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space including solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, and radios.

The Space Systems division has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. We have built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help get to space — our Space Systems division is empowering the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

PRINCIPAL PROGRAM MANAGER

Rocket Lab Optical Systems solves mission-critical space domain and Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance challenges for Department of Defense and Intelligence Community customers. Our vision is to revolutionize the space-based payload market with innovative and novel designs for space, terrestrial, and airborne environments. Building on more than 20 years of electro-optical and infrared systems innovation from Geost, Rocket Lab Optical Systems delivers solutions to the warfighter for responsive, scalable sensing solutions across all orbital domains.

As a Principal Program Manager for Rocket Lab Optical Systems in Tucson, AZ, you will lead EO/IR space missions and ground-based sensor networks, and the research. You must possess experience in managing programs including electronics, software, and EO/IR sensors on space or ground systems.

What You’ll Get To Do

Manage multiple contracts, ensuring cost, risk, schedule, staffing resources, and technical performance of company programs or subsystems of major programs, addressing any issues or risks that arise
Identify and mitigate potential risks to programs, develop contingency plans, develop and execute recovery plans, ensure timely resolution of issues, and track financial impacts
Work on unusually complex technical problems and provide innovative solutions
Lead team(s) of engineers in planning and executing test events and resolving issues encountered, both operational and technical
Work proactively to complete tasks and meet assigned deadlines with little direction
Build and deliver effective presentations to communicate program status and plans with little direction
Communicate effectively with team members across disciplines, with project management, and particularly with customers
Maintain clear and consistent communication and foster strong relationships with a wide range of internal stakeholders, particularly with functional teams and executive leadership
Build and maintain trusted relationships with key customers, partners, and stakeholders
Lead program and customer meetings and reviews
Lead technical interchange meetings with the team members and other project personnel and represent the organization in matters pertaining to project development
Lead and mentor junior technical staff and program support resources, providing guidance and support as needed
Develop and closely track Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) for projects and manage Earned Value Management (EVM) metrics (as required)
Support, and influence/lead where required, proposal and ECP efforts
Support travel or off-site work as needed
Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications You’ll Bring As Principal Program Manager

Bachelor’s degree in business, technology, or technical discipline
12+ years of experience in managing technical projects for the US Government
Proven ability to lead a team to the completion of programs and project milestones
Hands-on expertise with active optical systems
Experience with space EO payloads, test plan development, astronomy, physics, electronics, software, and/or remote sensing
Active Secret clearance with TS/SCI eligibility
U.S citizenship is required, due to program requirements

These Qualifications Would Be Nice To Have

Current SSBI clearance
Excellent communication and presentation skills
Self-motivated and capable of performing tasks with minimal oversight
Superior oral and written communication skills and sound problem-solving skills
Continuous improvement mindset and high attention to detail and accuracy
Experience performing and working in a dynamic and high-visibility role
Excellent management skills, including the ability to prioritize tasks, manage resources, and deliver results within given constraints
Internship or research experience supporting aerospace, defense, or optics-related projects
Exposure to MBSE concepts and tools such as Cameo Systems Modeler
Familiarity with environmental testing flight hardware
Experience with configuration management practices and systems engineering documentation
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including use of formulas and data analysis tools
Knowledge of astronomy, physics, imaging systems, or remote sensing

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

What To Expect

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important Information

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

jobs.title: Museum Program Manager
jobs.description:
Overview

Join our team as a Museum Program Manager and support the U.S. Coast Guard's new National Coast Guard Museum in New London, Connecticut by leading the contractor team that runs day-to-day museum operations. You will direct visitor services, education, volunteer, events and IT/AV support staff, ensure a safe, welcoming, world-class experience for an expected 300,000 visitors a year.

FWI is expanding rapidly and has been recognized as a 2024, 2025 and 2026 Top Workplace, offering excellent growth opportunities in a collaborative environment.

Position is contingent upon contract award**

Work Schedule and Location:

On-Site:
Full-time, onsite at the National Coast Guard Museum in New London, CT; candidates must live within a reasonable daily commute (about 50 miles). The museum is open 363 days a year, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM, so occasional weekend, holiday and evening presence is expected. No travel required.

Responsibilities

Lead a 16-person on-site team across visitor services, education, volunteers, events, IT/AV and exhibit maintenance.
Serve as the primary liaison to the U.S. Coast Guard for performance, staffing and contract matters.
Manage staffing costs, invoicing, performance records and quality control.
Keep galleries and technical systems covered every day the museum is open, 363 days a year.
Build standard operating procedures, annual work plans and KPIs from the museum's strategic goals.
Stand up the team during a 30-day launch period: hiring, onboarding, training and readiness.

Required

Qualifications

Bachelor's or master's degree in museum studies, art history, business administration, public administration, or a related field.
7+ years of progressively responsible leadership in a museum, cultural institution, public attraction, or similar nonprofit, including at least 3 years managing budgets and personnel.
Experience with personnel and performance management, operating budgets, and museum back-of-house operations (collections care, exhibition production, facilities).
Ability to pass a federal Tier 1 Public Trust background investigation.

Desired

Experience running a museum, or knowledge of U.S. Coast Guard history and missions.
Crisis and risk management experience, from facility emergencies to public relations issues.
Experience implementing collection management systems or digital visitor-engagement tools.
A track record of bridging curatorial and administrative teams.

At FWI, we place the highest importance on creating an exceptional employee experience. jobs.description:
Job Description:

At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection. We do this by driving Responsible Growth and delivering for our clients, teammates, communities and shareholders every day.

Being a Great Place to Work and providing a culture of caring is core to how we drive Responsible Growth. We are intentional about fostering an inclusive workplace where every teammate has the opportunity to succeed, build a career and contribute to our shared success. This includes attracting and developing exceptional talent, recognizing and rewarding performance, and supporting our teammates’ physical, emotional, and financial wellness through affordable, competitive and flexible benefits.

We value the unique perspectives individuals bring from all backgrounds and career paths - whether shaped by military service, community college education, or a wide range of work and life experiences. These journeys foster resilience, leadership and innovation, strengthening our workforce and positively impact the communities we serve.

Bank of America is committed to an in-office culture that supports collaboration, engagement, and career development. Our approach includes clear in-office expectations, while providing an appropriate level of flexibility based on role-specific responsibilities and business needs.

At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. Join us!

Job Description:

The Investigations Manager is responsible for leading, coaching, and developing a team of Investigations Analysts. This role oversees investigative quality, productivity, and risk management while ensuring adherence to regulatory requirements and enterprise standards. Successful candidates demonstrate strong leadership, sound judgment, and effective decision-making. They balance operational performance with employee development and are comfortable partnering with multiple stakeholders.

Responsibilities

Lead, coach, and develop a team of investigators to meet production, quality, and service level expectations.
Provide guidance on complex investigations, suspicious activity assessments, and escalation decisions.
Review investigative findings to ensure documentation is accurate, thorough, and compliant with regulatory and enterprise requirements.
Support the timely and accurate completion of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) for submission to regulators and/or law enforcement.
Monitor team performance and drive accountability for quality, productivity, and risk management standards.
Conduct quality reviews and provide coaching to support employee development.
Partner with senior leaders and business stakeholders to communicate investigative trends, risks, and case outcomes.
Identify and implement process improvements that enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness.

Required Qualifications

Demonstrated leadership capabilities with the ability to coach, develop, and motivate others.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to effectively present findings and recommendations.
Excellent analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to make sound, risk-based decisions in a fast-paced environment.
Flexible and adaptable with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities.
Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Proven ability to collaborate and build relationships across teams and organizational levels.
Technical proficiency with the ability to quickly learn and navigate multiple investigative systems and tools.
Demonstrated sense of urgency, accountability, and attention to detail.

Desired Qualifications

3+ years of experience in Anti-Money Laundering, Financial Crimes, Fraud, Investigations, or related risk management functions.
Prior leadership, mentoring, or workflow coordination experience.
Experience providing feedback, coaching, and performance guidance.
Familiarity with transaction monitoring and case management systems.
CAMS certification or willingness to obtain certification.

Skills

People Leadership & Team Development
Professional curiosity and investigative mindset
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills
Attention to Detail and accuracy
Ability to synthesize large amounts of data from multiple sources
Sound risk judgment and escalation discipline
Strong written communication skills
Effective time management and organizational skills
Technical proficiency and the ability to quickly learn and navigate multiple investigative systems and tools simultaneously
Regulatory Compliance
Adherence to policies, procedures, and guidelines
Adaptability & Commitment to Continuous Improvement

Shift:

1st shift (United States of America)

Hours Per Week:

40

jobs.description:
It's more than a job

As part of the Contract Logistics team at Kuehne+Nagel, you will play a key role in designing, managing, and optimizing solutions that keep goods moving efficiently. Whether you’re leading a team, engineering processes, or driving projects, your work ensures that our customers’ products are stored, handled, and delivered with precision. From everyday essentials to seasonal items, what we do in Contract Logistics impacts businesses and communities around the world. At Kuehne+Nagel, your contribution goes far beyond the warehouse—it helps shape the flow of global trade.

‎

Take the lead on complex IS/IT implementations and system migrations that make a real business impact.
You’ll bring together cross-functional project teams, manage priorities and timelines, anticipate and resolve risks, oversee project budgets, and ensure a seamless experience for both clients and internal stakeholders.

Lead cross-functional IT project teams supporting customer implementations, system migrations, strategic initiatives, and organizational change.
Serve as the IT project or sub-project lead for customer onboarding initiatives, coordinating activities across IT, Operations, Engineering, and external partners.

Manage vendors and client relationships, ensuring external partners meet delivery, cost, and SOW commitments while serving as a key point of contact for customer change management.

Degree in Logistics, Engineering, or Business Management or equivalent work experience
5 years of project management experience leading WMS system implementation projects required, experience with JDA/Blue Yonder or Manhattan an advantage.
Experience in a 3PL environment required
PMP certification or similar desired

Ability to travel 50% during project execution, depending on project phase.
Proven ability to manage large system implementation teams including external resources.
Excellent interpersonal, facilitation and communication skills.

Logistics shapes everyday life - from the goods we consume to the healthcare we rely on. At Kuehne+Nagel, your work goes beyond logistics; it enables both ordinary and special moments in the lives of people around the world.

As a global leader with a strong heritage and a vision to move the world forward, we offer a safe, stable environment where your career can make a real difference. jobs.title: Implementation Manager - Quote to Order
jobs.description:
At ABB, we help industries outrun - leaner and cleaner. Here, progress is an expectation - for you, your team, and the world. As a global market leader, we’ll give you what you need to make it happen. It won’t always be easy, growing takes grit. But at ABB, you’ll never run alone. Run what runs the world.

This role sits within ABB's Robotics business, a leading global robotics company. We're entering an exciting new chapter as we’ve announced the plan for SoftBank Group to acquire ABB Robotics. SoftBank is a globally recognized technology group and investor/operator focused on AI, robotics, and next-generation computing. By joining us now, you’ll be part of a pioneering team shaping the future of robotics—working alongside world-class experts in a fast-moving, innovation-driven environment.

This Position Reports To

Business Process Manager

We Are Hiring 3 Implementation Managers To Drive Our Global Quote-to-Order Transformation. You Will Join a Key Initiative To Standardize Commercial Processes And Digital Solutions Across Our Business. Apply For The Region That Matches Your Profile And Career Aspirations

Europe — Flexible location across European countries
America — Flexible location across American countries
Asia — Flexible location across Asia (excl. China)

Each role is autonomous and high-impact, with direct influence on how our commercial operations work in your region.

About The Role

Join ABB Robotics as an Implementation Manager and drive the implementation and adoption of our global Quote-to-Order process and supporting digital solutions.

The role will work closely with country commercial organizations to understand their current ways of working, introduce the global Quote-to-Order process, identify gaps and local requirements, and support countries through the transition to the target process and tools. The current solution landscape includes CPQ and the commercial Quote-to-Order processes interfacing with SAP S/4HANA
, together with other supporting applications. The scope may evolve as the Quote-to-Order process and application landscape develops. The position is part of the Commercial Excellence – Quote to Order Process
organization and reports to the Quote to Order Process Manager
.

This is a high-impact, cross-functional role at the heart of our commercial transformation.

What You Will Do

Lead implementation of the global Quote-to-Order process across your region.
Facilitate workshops to map current country processes against the global target, identify gaps, and define how they are resolved.
Support countries through a complete tool landscape transformation — you'll be equally comfortable helping teams understand new processes and navigating new tools.
Act as the primary business process advisor and second-level tool support contact for your region's countries — balancing process discipline with pragmatic tool troubleshooting
Coordinate deployment of CPQ and related solutions, including the commercial process integration and handover into SAP S/4HANA.
Act as the primary Quote-to-Order implementation contact for your region’s countries, building trusted relationships with sales organizations and key stakeholders.
Build strong relationships with country Sales organizations and key stakeholders. Understand existing country commercial processes, requirements and ways of working and support countries through the change management process.
Define and execute country implementation plans covering preparation, testing, training, go-live and stabilization. Coordinate user acceptance testing and implementation readiness with countries and IT/IS teams.
Champion continuous improvement post go-live, translating recurring business challenges into structured requirements for process and tool enhancements.

What You Bring

3-5 years of proven experience in commercial process implementation, digital transformation or business change roles in a B2B environment.
Good understanding of commercial processes such as quotation, pricing, configuration, sales operations or order handling.
Experience working with commercial platforms such as CPQ, CRM, CLM or ERP is an advantage.
Experience with commercial processes integrated with SAP S/4HANA or comparable ERP environments is an advantage.
Strong stakeholder management and facilitation skills. You are equally confident with business and technical audiences.
Experience working across multiple countries and in matrix organizations; structured, self-driven and ownership-oriented.
Fluent in English; local or regional language skills are an advantage. Willingness to travel frequently within your region, particularly during implementation phases.

The Ideal Candidate

You combine commercial understanding, process orientation and change management expertise. You know how to sit with a country team, understand how they work today, and guide them confidently toward a standardized global process, without losing sight of legitimate local needs. You do not need to be a Process Owner, CPQ specialist or ERP expert, but you must have enough breadth across commercial, process and systems topics to lead implementation to successful adoption.

Compensation Package

For candidates applying from Italy:

As part of our commitment to transparency, we want to share the compensation details for this position:

Applicable CBA: Metalmeccanico

Minimum annual salary: €53.000

Variable Pay: AIP target % + Eligible for Company Productivity Bonus

Country-specific benefits will be discussed with shortlisted candidates based on location.

The offer will be tailored based on your role location, experience, skills and qualifications, internal market positioning and alignment with ABB internal standards.

Benefits As Per Policy

Flexible working hours, hybrid work options, and a strong focus on work-life integration and Wellbeing support for employees and their families

Welfare plan with a wide range of personalized services

Canteen or meal vouchers provided

We value people from different backgrounds. Could this be your story? Apply today or visit www.abb.com to read more about us and learn about the impact of our solutions across the globe.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

The State Government Finance and System Project Manager leads public-sector modernization engagements. This role serves as a trusted advisor embedded within state, county, and municipal agencies to drive enterprise software initiatives, business process optimizations, and strategic IT transformations. The Project Manager manages client relationships, directs cross-functional project teams, and ensures the successful delivery of varying client-side milestones across multiple simultaneous or sequential engagements.

Job Duties

Provides project management support for client project management teams leading software selection, implementations, and system integrations
Handles core systems and staff augmentation roles
Develops, builds, and revises procedures and client playbooks for system rollouts
Helps to protect clients from vendor scope creep and monitors project risks
Oversees documentation, project timelines, and internal and vendor-facing deliverables
Other duties as required to support changing client needs across different agency engagements

Supervisory Responsibilities

Supervises, develops, and trains Project Manager Associates and Senior Associates
Reviews and evaluates work of the Associates and Senior Associates
Provides verbal and written performance feedback to Associates and Senior Associates

Education

Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Bachelor’s degree, required; focus in Business, Accounting or Finance, preferred

Experience

Five (5) or more years of experience in project management, required
Familiar with ERP systems & technology implementation best practices (eg. Infor, Workday, Netsuite, Tyler, OpenGov, etc.), preferred
Experience with State and Local Government, nonprofit, and other highly regulated industries, preferred

License/Certifications

CAPM or PMP, required
SmartSheet certifications, preferred

Software

Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office suite, specifically Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, required
SmartSheet experience, preferred
SharePoint experience, preferred

Language

N/A

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, specifically business / report writing
Strong analytical and basic research skills
Solid organizational skills, especially the ability to meet project deadlines with a focus on details
Ability to successfully multi-task while working independently or within a group environment
Ability to work in a deadline-driven environment and handle multiple projects simultaneously
Ability to work with minimal supervision

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Work Location

Edmonton Corporate Office

About The Role

Reporting to the SVP, Business Transformation PMO, the Project Manager will lead the planning, execution, and successful delivery of cross-functional projects. Working closely with business leaders, project teams, and key stakeholders to define project objectives, establish clear plans, manage timelines and budgets, and ensure deliverables meet business requirements and quality standards.

You will provide hands-on leadership throughout the project lifecycle, proactively manage risks and dependencies, and maintain clear communication to keep projects aligned and on track. Project governance and documentation must be proportionate to project size, risk and aligned with EPMO standards.

Role And Responsibilities

Lead projects from initiation through implementation and closeout, ensuring delivery within approved scope, timelines, and budget.
Partner with business leaders and stakeholders to define project objectives, requirements, deliverables, and success measures.
Develop and maintain integrated project plans with work breakdowns, task owners, effort estimates, milestones, dependencies, critical paths, and approved schedule baselines; assess slippage and maintain recovery plans.
Establish proportionate project governance, a RACI matrix, decision and approval authorities, escalation paths, and delivery gates in alignment with EPMO standards.
Manage project budgets, forecasts, resource allocation, and financial reporting, escalating variances as required.
Coordinate cross-functional project teams and external partners to ensure accountability and timely completion of deliverables.
Establish and lead a consistent project cadence, including weekly delivery meetings and status updates, sponsor reviews, and steering committee meetings appropriate to project needs. Issue agendas, record decisions and actions with owners and due dates, and follow through to closure.
Provide accurate, evidence-based status reporting covering milestone progress, budget and forecast, resource capacity, risks, issues, dependencies, and decisions required. Explain variances and corrective actions; avoid reporting a project as on track when evidence indicates otherwise.
Maintain a current risk, issue, assumption, and dependency log with owners, mitigation actions, due dates, and escalation triggers. Identify cross-project dependencies and escalate emerging threats early, with options and a recommended course of action.
Manage scope and change requests through documented impact analysis covering cost, schedule, resources, dependencies, and benefits; obtain required approvals before changing baselines or committing additional work.
Investigate delivery challenges, hold action owners accountable, and drive corrective and recovery plans. Escalate unresolved barriers or overdue decisions promptly through agreed governance channels.
Independently create and maintain the required project documentation from inception through closure: charter, scope and requirements, integrated plan, budget and forecast, resource plan and RACI, stakeholder and communication plan, risk and issue log, action and decision logs, status reports, change requests, acceptance records, and closure report. Keep documents current, version-controlled, and accessible in the designated repository.
Coordinate business readiness, stakeholder engagement, communications, training, and adoption activities with business owners and change management leads; define readiness criteria and surface adoption risks before implementation.
Define deliverable acceptance criteria and coordinate quality reviews, testing and user acceptance testing where applicable. Obtain documented business sign-off and confirm operational readiness before recommending go-live or closure.
Maintain resource mapping across assigned projects, showing required skills, named resources, estimated effort, availability, and allocation over time. Validate capacity with functional leaders, identify over-allocation and conflicting priorities, and recommend sequencing or staffing adjustments before committing delivery dates.
Select and apply appropriate predictive, agile, or hybrid delivery methods within EPMO standards; tailor controls to the project while maintaining clear accountability and traceability.
Complete formal project closeout, including business acceptance, budget reconciliation, lessons learned, documentation handover, and transition to operational owners with support responsibilities and outstanding actions. Agree benefit measures, baselines, and post-implementation review ownership with the sponsor.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of project management processes, templates, tools, and governance practices.
Provide coaching and guidance to project team members and stakeholders on project management expectations and practices.
Manage external delivery partners against agreed statements of work, milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria; validate deliverables and flag scope gaps, performance concerns, or additional charges before commitments are made.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Project Management, or a related field; an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Minimum of 5 years of progressive project management experience, including responsibility for leading cross-functional projects.
Demonstrated experience independently leading cross-functional projects from initiation through implementation and closeout, with examples of results achieved against agreed scope, schedule, budget, and business outcomes.
Strong knowledge of project management methodologies, governance practices, tools, and best practices.
Proven ability to independently build and maintain project charters, integrated schedules, budgets and forecasts, resource plans, governance materials, risk and issue logs, status reports, and executive presentations; practical delivery experience is essential.
Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent projects with shared resources, validate team capacity, negotiate priorities with functional leaders, and resolve competing demands.
Proficiency with project scheduling and collaboration tools and Microsoft Office, including Excel and PowerPoint; able to build dependency-based schedules, resource views, and clear management reporting.
Experience supporting change management, process improvement, or business transformation initiatives is an asset.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is preferred. Certification must be supported by demonstrated hands-on delivery experience and the ability to apply project management practices in a lean, evolving organization.
Experience in a complex, multi-business, retail, manufacturing, or regulated environment is an asset.
Experience recovering delayed or at-risk projects, including root-cause assessment, re-planning, stakeholder alignment, and sustained follow-through.

What Makes SNDL a Great Place To Grow

Competitive compensation including performance-based bonuses and annual salary reviews.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits, including a Healthcare Spending Account.
Three weeks of paid vacation with annual rollover.
Flexible, hybrid work arrangements to support work-life balance.
Recognition and rewards programs that celebrate individual and team achievements.
Employee & Family Assistance Program (EFAP) with mental health, financial, and family support.
Employee perks and discounts program, offering savings across fitness, wellness, lifestyle, retail, and everyday services

We are grateful for the interest in this role from all candidates, however, we will be contacting only those that are selected for next steps in the hiring process.

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

SNDL is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a welcoming, inclusive, diverse and safe workplace where all of our team members have equal opportunity to succeed. We know this begins with recruitment. To honor our commitment, SNDL encourages applications from individuals of all backgrounds, sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, ages and abilities.
