Position Overview

The Senior Marketing Intelligence Analyst is the tactical data and analytical partner to the Strategic Marketing Team, keeping data at the forefront of every campaign, initiative, and business decision. This role is responsible for proactively analyzing marketing performance, strategically recommending improvements, and ensuring data accuracy from the first project idea through after-action reporting. Working closely with strategic marketing leadership, engineering, and external vendors, the Senior Marketing Intelligence Analyst translates complex data into clear, actionable recommendations that drive revenue, improve client experience, and sharpen how CCM markets at scale. This role leverages modern AI tools to accelerate report creation, optimize analysis, and deliver insights faster, empowering CCM to make data-driven decisions with confidence.

Job Responsibilities

Partner with the Strategic Marketing Team on initiatives during the planning stage to support goal setting, validate assumptions, and define success metrics.
Analyze marketing performance across paid, owned, and earned channels (e.g., search, social media, email, display, servicing, and content) to identify trends, anomalies, and opportunities ahead of stakeholder requests.
Strategically recommend improvements based on data, providing clear, actionable guidance to strategic marketing leadership and campaign teams.
Evaluate ROI across marketing campaigns, channels, and strategies to identify the highest-returning initiatives and recommend where to concentrate investment to maximize impact.
Ensure data accuracy and integrity from project initiation through after-action reporting, catching issues early and documenting data lineage across marketing datasets.
Design, develop, and maintain self-service marketing dashboards in Sigma, Tableau, or Power BI, ensuring data is accurate, refreshed, and accessible to non-technical stakeholders.
Deliver weekly and monthly performance reports to strategic marketing leadership with clear narrative, KPI scorecards, and recommended actions, leveraging AI tools to accelerate report drafting and executive summaries.
Build and maintain attribution models including last touch, linear, and data driven approaches to evaluate the true contribution of each marketing channel to pipeline and revenue.
Develop customer segmentation and cohort analyses to guide targeting, personalization, and lifecycle marketing strategies.
Partner with vendors and data engineers to define requirements for marketing data pipelines, resolve data quality issues at the source, and document data lineage.
Support A/B and multivariate test design, analysis, and read-out across campaigns and digital experiences.
Leverage AI and machine learning tools to optimize workflows, including drafting SQL, exploring datasets, generating hypotheses, and stress-testing recommendations.
Act as the analytics subject-matter expert for marketing operations and demand generation, answering ad-hoc questions and upskilling stakeholders on data and AI best practices.
Stay current on emerging analytics platforms, AI tools, and marketing measurement best practices to drive innovation and continuous improvement.
Ensure all analytics practices comply with industry’s best practices and legal/regulatory requirements, including CAN-SPAM, GDPR, and CCPA.

Qualifications And Skills

Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of experience and certifications in marketing analytics, business intelligence, data analytics, or a related field.
4+ years of experience in marketing analytics, business intelligence, data analyst, or marketing intelligence roles.
Experience translating analysis into strategic recommendations that have influenced business decisions.
Experience using analytics and AI tools (e.g., Claude, Microsoft Copilot, or similar tools) to draft reports, write and debug code, summarize findings, and build lightweight automations.
Knowledge of Python or R for data manipulation and exploratory analysis.
Knowledge of data privacy regulations including GDPR and CCPA, and best practices for data quality and lineage documentation.
Familiarity with digital marketing platforms such as Google Analytics 4, Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, and CRM systems.
Familiarity with attribution modeling, marketing mix modeling, or incrementality testing, preferred.
Understanding of statistical concepts including hypothesis testing, statistical significance, and regression basics.
Understanding of customer data platforms and how event data flows between systems, preferred.
Advanced proficiency with at least one business intelligence platform, such as Sigma, Tableau, or Power BI.
Proficiency working in cloud data warehouses such as Snowflake, including writing strong SQL for data exploration and reporting.
Excellent data storytelling skills, including presenting complex findings clearly and concisely to non-technical and executive audiences.
Excellent critical thinking skills and attention to detail.
Excellent collaboration and communication skills, working effectively with individuals at all levels of an organization.
Skilled in problem-solving and performing effectively in deadline-driven environments.

The Security Analyst is a hands-on role that will play an integral role in the active defense of the systems and networks at the agency. The Security Analyst will support the establishment, implementation and/or enhancement of Information Systems' Security and Compliance efforts based on Federal, State and Agency Policy/Standards. HELP SHAPE THE FUTURE OF CANCER CARE IN CANADA

The Canadian Cancer Society works tirelessly to save lives, improve lives and drive collective action against cancer. Together with patients, volunteers, donors and communities across the country, we raise funds to invest in transformative cancer research, we provide a caring support system for everyone affected by cancer and we advocate to governments to create a healthier future for all. It takes a society to take on cancer – and the Canadian Cancer Society is leading the way.

MAKING AN IMPACT

Reporting to the Director, Surveillance, the Surveillance Program Manager plays a critical role in leading the operational delivery, coordination and continuous improvement of the Canadian Cancer Society's surveillance and cancer statistics programs. The role is responsible for managing complex multi-partner initiatives, supporting national advisory committee and working group structures, overseeing the production and dissemination of flagship surveillance products, coordinating external vendor and partner relationships, and ensuring efficient program operations.

The Program Manager serves as a key point of contact for the Canadian Cancer Society’s national surveillance portfolio, including the Canadian Cancer Statistics program, implementation of the pan-Canadian Cancer Data Strategy and the Data Transformation grant program. The Program Manager works with key external collaborators including Statistics Canada, the Public Health Agency of Canada, the Canadian Partnership Against Cancer, provincial and territorial cancer registries, academic experts and volunteers, people with lived and living experience, as well as internal CCS teams to ensure high-quality surveillance products are delivered on time and with impact. The Program Manager provides enabling support to the Director, Surveillance, to expand key relationships with national and international collaborators and interest holders.

What You’ll Be Doing

Program Implementation and Management
Manage end-to-end implementation of multi-interest holder cancer surveillance and data programs and projects, including operational planning, coordination, monitoring and knowledge translation.
Develop and maintain integrated workplans, production schedules, risk logs, and reporting processes across Surveillance initiatives.
Manage the governance and operations of the Canadian Cancer Statistics Advisory Committee, including meeting planning, logistics, agendas, minutes, action-item tracking and committee communications, as well as the nomination process for members and chairs.
Coordinate monthly collaborator meetings, semi-annual senior collaborator meetings and strategic working groups, including methods, evaluation and special report subcommittees.
Lead production management for Canadian Cancer Statistics publications, special reports and knowledge translation products from planning through publication and evaluation.
Manage additional surveillance-related publication production workflows involving authors, reviewers, copyeditors, graphic designers, translators and publication vendors.
Support the Surveillance leadership in preparing for and executing follow-up actions from meetings, including development of communications, presentations, conference abstracts, reporting compilation, among others.
Lead the development and continuous improvement of project management processes, standard operating procedures, templates, and tools to support the Surveillance team and improve efficiency and quality.
Delegate coordination of administrative project deliverables to various Surveillance and CCS staff to deliver knowledge products and events.
Provide mentorship to Surveillance staff to build capacity and support career development.
Relationship Management and Interest-holder Engagement
Build and maintain strong working relationships with federal collaborators (Statistics Canada, the Public Health Agency of Canada), academic collaborators and advisors, provincial and territorial cancer registries, researchers, contractors, people with lived and living experience, and volunteer experts.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal teams (e.g., Fundraising; Communications; Digital Engagement; Digital Marketing and Solutions; Data Strategy, Analytics and Solutions; Advocacy and Health Policy; Research; Cancer Information; Cancer Prevention; Cancer Strategy and Innovation) to ensure alignment and collaboration to maximize impact and reach of Surveillance products.
Support relationship building with key international collaborators and interest holders, including, but not limited to, the International Agency for Research on Cancer, international and regional cancer registries, global health organizations (e.g., WHO), among others.
Manage communications and engagement activities leading up to publication releases, including webinars, briefings and pre-release meetings.
Lead the execution of launch activities, including strategic kick-off events and collaborative planning sessions that align internal and external interest-holders with CCS’s priorities.
Coordinate interest-holder outreach and dissemination activities for surveillance publications, reports and knowledge products.
Support preparation of briefing notes, presentations, reports, committee materials and executive updates for CCS leadership.
Financial and Administrative Management
Manage Surveillance program budgets, contracts, invoices, expense claims and vendor agreements.
Coordinate vendor procurement and relationships, including translation, graphic design, editing and digital platform providers, as required.
Monitor budget performance and support annual planning and forecasting activities.
Maintain Surveillance SharePoint resources, program records and documentation systems.
Coordinate administrative processes that support effective delivery of the Surveillance portfolio.
Coordinate updates to cancer.ca and related digital dissemination channels for Surveillance content.
Other
Foster a high-performance culture that leverages the unique talents and strengths of each member while encouraging their growth and development.
Champion CCS as a hero in the face of cancer.
Contribute to our culture of diversity, inclusion, belonging and equity (DIBE) by ensuring that all staff feel represented, valued, and heard across all aspects of their identity, including gender, age, religion, ethnicity, nationality, race, and sexuality.
Other duties as assigned

5+ years - extensive job-related experience in progressively more senior positions.

Experience supporting committees, advisory groups or governance structures.

Experience with budget administration.

jobs.description:

About Us

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We ensure that whatever the building, its design is outstanding, and its operations meet the needs of the communities it serves.

We are as committed to providing an environment where everyone can realise their unique potential. So, in joining Hoare Lea, you will experience a business that enriches your knowledge, supports your wellbeing, and welcomes your individuality. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in our 9-day fortnight scheme, thriving community groups, varied social and networking events, and extensive professional and technical development schemes. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, an electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and 25 days of annual leave (increasing with service), alongside flexible and hybrid working.

Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.

About The Role

Our multi-disciplinary software, product, and data team serves as a central hub of digital expertise and innovation, supporting projects across the company. We work collaboratively with engineers, consultants and other specialists to use data and technology to solve real-world problems and improve the services we provide to our clients.

We have an opportunity for a Data Analyst/Scientist or Senior Data Analyst/Scientist to play a key role in using data, analytics, statistical methods and data science to generate insight, support decision-making and improve our engineering services.

This is a broad analytical role. You will work across the full lifecycle of a problem: understanding stakeholder needs, exploring and assessing data, identifying appropriate analytical approaches, communicating findings and, where appropriate, developing statistical or machine-learning models or client-ready insights/tools. This is a role for someone who enjoys variety and has a critical eye for finding the right solution for the problem. Sometimes this may be exploratory analysis, a dashboard or a set of clearly defined metrics; in other cases, it may involve forecasting, statistical modelling, machine learning or building/working with AI.

It's an exciting time to join our Digital team. Working alongside a range of specialist engineers and consultants, you will be joining a collaborative, knowledgeable, highly engaged team, and offer a supportive, flexible, and high-performing work culture. In a time where building and energy resilience is ever more important, we are driving forward innovation to make an impact with data and technology.

You will have the opportunity to engage in a variety of high-impact projects, working on challenging problems for some of the UK’s most notable organisations, including the NHS and Oxford University. Our team has recently worked on creating data science-led for managing estates in hospitals, building energy forecasting models, and harnessing data on building performance to create better designed buildings of the future.

In this key and varied role, you can expect to:

Work with engineers, consultants, product teams and other stakeholders to understand their needs and translate sometimes ambiguous questions into well-defined analytical problems.
Develop and implement data-driven solutions to solve real-world business problems across the company.
Use SQL, Python and other analytical tools to investigate datasets, identify trends and relationships, test hypotheses and generate actionable insights.
Apply appropriate statistical techniques, forecasting methods, ML and AI approaches where they add value to the problem being solved.
Collaborate with the product and software engineering teams to turn analytical work into reusable tools, workflows and data-driven products where appropriate.
Develop reproducible and maintainable analytical code, following best practices, including version control, testing, and peer reviews.
Contribute to the development of analytical and data science capability across the business by sharing approaches, reusable methods and good practice

About You

To be successful in this role you’ll need:

Essential Skills

Experience applying data and analysis to real-world business, engineering or operational problems.
Strong analytical problem-solving skills, with the ability to take an initially ambiguous question and determine an appropriate analytical approach.
Ability to work on projects independently and own deliverables.
Strong proficiency in Python for data manipulation, analysis, visualisation and data science (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn).
Proficiency in data querying languages (e.g., SQL). Solid understanding of software engineering best practices (version control, unit testing, code review, etc.).
Strong experience with data visualisation frameworks (e.g., PowerBI, Streamlit).
Experience applying machine learning and AI, including generative AI, to real-world problems where it provides clear benefit.
Familiarity with statistical concepts and their application in data analysis.
Solid communication skills, capable of effectively engaging with and presenting findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Understanding of data governance, privacy, responsible AI and other relevant standards.

Desirable Skills

Knowledge of the engineering industry and its challenges.
Experience with one of the major machine learning frameworks (TensorFlow or PyTorch).
Knowledge of mathematical optimisation methods, such as linear, integer or constraint optimisation, and associated tools (e.g. OR-Tools).
Experience with MS Fabric or equivalent data warehousing solution.
Experience working in a cloud computing environment.
Familiarity with containerisation and deployment technologies (e.g., Docker, CI/CD pipelines).

For candidates joining at Senior
level, we would additionally expect you to lead more complex or ambiguous analytical projects, shape analytical approaches and overarching priorities, work independently with senior stakeholders, review and support the work of others, and help raise analytical standards across the team.

How To Apply

To apply simply complete a CV profile and submit your application.

If shortlisted, one of our recruitment team will be in touch to arrange an introductory call (about 30 minutes) to discuss the role and your experience in more detail. From there, successful candidates will be invited to attend a panel interview, either via Microsoft Teams or in person at one of our offices. We aim to provide feedback at each stage of the process.

Adjustments and accommodations

If there are adjustments or accommodations that we can put in place to help you participate and give your best at any stage of the recruitment process (whether relating to disability, neurodivergence or anything else) please let us know.

jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day

As a Data Analytics & BI Developer Employee within Siemens Energy's Montreal Digitalization team, you will turn complex manufacturing, engineering, and business data into scalable analytics solutions. Your day may include designing Snowflake data models, building Matillion pipelines, troubleshooting data quality issues, integrating SAP data, and developing Power BI or Tableau dashboards that help stakeholders make informed decisions. You will collaborate with business and technical colleagues, contributing to practical digital solutions that improve reporting, operational visibility, and process optimization across the organization.

How You’ll Make An Impact

Design dimensional and analytical data models using star and snowflake schemas, and build scalable, reliable data pipelines for analytics and business intelligence initiatives.
Develop and optimize advanced SQL queries, views, stored procedures, and Snowflake data models, using Matillion to deliver robust reporting and analytics solutions.
Use AWS cloud services for data storage and computation, including SQS queues, SNS notifications, and Lambda functions.
Create and maintain interactive Power BI and Tableau dashboards that translate operational data into clear, actionable insights.
Model complex SAP ECC or S/4HANA transactional data in Snowflake, and develop or maintain ASP.NET applications that support data integration and reporting needs.
Collaborate with business stakeholders to gather requirements, define KPIs, and deliver solutions in an Agile Scrum environment using Jira and Confluence.

What You Bring

At least three years of full-time experience in Business Intelligence, Data Engineering, or Analytics Engineering, supported by expert-level SQL development skills.
Strong experience with Snowflake data warehousing, ETL/ELT processes, Matillion, AWS cloud services, and scalable data pipeline development.
Hands-on experience analyzing and modeling SAP ECC or S/4HANA data and transforming transactional information into business-friendly analytical models.
Experience with Power BI and/or Tableau; additional knowledge of DAX, ASP.NET, Python, Git, machine learning, or large language models is considered an asset.
Strong communication, collaboration, and business engagement skills, with experience working in Agile Scrum teams; manufacturing or energy industry experience is preferred.

About The Team

Siemens Energy’s Digitalization team in Montreal develops data-driven solutions that support the manufacturing of new engines and Repair & Overhaul (R&O) operations. The team works closely with manufacturing, engineering, quality, and business stakeholders to improve operational visibility, optimize processes, and support informed decision-making. You will join a collaborative, cross-functional environment focused on delivering practical digital solutions that create measurable value across the entire engine lifecycle.

Who is Siemens Energy?

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Analyste de données et développeur BI

Un aperçu de votre journée

À titre d’employé(e) en analyse de données et développement BI au sein de l’équipe de numérisation de Siemens Energy à Montréal, vous transformerez des données complexes provenant des secteurs manufacturiers, de l’ingénierie et des opérations en solutions analytiques évolutives. Votre quotidien pourra inclure la conception de modèles de données dans Snowflake, le développement de pipelines Matillion, la résolution de problèmes de qualité des données, l’intégration de données SAP ainsi que la création de tableaux de bord Power BI ou Tableau permettant aux parties prenantes de prendre des décisions éclairées. Vous collaborerez étroitement avec des collègues d’affaires et techniques afin de développer des solutions numériques concrètes améliorant les capacités de suivi, la visibilité opérationnelle et l’optimisation des processus au sein de l’organisation.

Comment vous ferez la différence

Concevoir des modèles de données dimensionnels et analytiques à l’aide de schémas en étoile (star schema) et en flocon (snowflake schema), et développer des pipelines de données évolutifs et fiables pour soutenir les initiatives d’analytique et d’intelligence d’affaires.
Développer et optimiser des requêtes SQL avancées, des vues, des procédures stockées et des modèles de données Snowflake, en utilisant Matillion pour livrer des solutions robustes de production de rapports et d’analytique.

Créer et maintenir des tableaux de bord interactifs dans Power BI et Tableau afin de transformer les données opérationnelles en informations claires et exploitables.
Modéliser des données transactionnelles complexes provenant de SAP ECC ou SAP S/4HANA dans Snowflake, et développer ou maintenir des applications ASP.NET soutenant les besoins d’intégration de données et de production de rapports.

Au moins trois années d’expérience à temps plein dans les domaines de l’intelligence d’affaires (BI), de l’ingénierie des données (Data Engineering) ou de l’ingénierie analytique (Analytics Engineering), appuyées par une expertise avancée en développement SQL.
Solide expérience avec l’entreposage de données Snowflake, les processus ETL/ELT, Matillion, les services infonuagiques AWS et le développement de pipelines de données évolutifs.
Expérience pratique dans l’analyse et la modélisation des données SAP ECC ou SAP S/4HANA, ainsi que dans la transformation de données transactionnelles en modèles analytiques adaptés aux besoins d’affaires.
Expérience avec Power BI et/ou Tableau; des connaissances supplémentaires en DAX, ASP.NET, Python, Git, apprentissage automatique (Machine Learning) ou grands modèles de langage (LLM) constituent un atout.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication, en collaboration et en partenariat avec les clients internes, ainsi qu’une expérience au sein d’équipes Agile Scrum; une expérience dans les secteurs manufacturier ou de l’énergie est considérée comme un atout.

À propos de l’équipe 

L’équipe de numérisation de Siemens Energy à Montréal développe des solutions axées sur les données qui soutiennent les activités de fabrication de nouveaux moteurs ainsi que les opérations de réparation et maintenance. L’équipe collabore étroitement avec les groupes de fabrication, d’ingénierie, de qualité et d’affaires afin d’améliorer la visibilité opérationnelle, d’optimiser les processus et de soutenir une prise de décision éclairée. Vous évoluerez dans un environnement collaboratif et multidisciplinaire où les solutions numériques concrètes contribuent à créer une valeur mesurable tout au long du cycle de vie des moteurs. 

Qui est Siemens Energy ?

Chez Siemens Energy, nous sommes plus qu’une simple entreprise de technologie énergétique. Avec environ 100 000 employés dévoués dans plus de 90 pays, nous développons les systèmes énergétiques de demain, garantissant que la demande énergétique croissante de la communauté mondiale soit satisfaite de manière fiable et durable. Les technologies créées dans nos départements de recherche et nos usines propulsent la transition énergétique et constituent la base d’un sixième de la production mondiale d’électricité.

Notre équipe mondiale s’engage à faire d’une énergie durable, fiable et abordable une réalité en repoussant les limites de ce qui est possible. Nous préservons un héritage de 150 ans d’innovation qui nous encourage à rechercher des personnes qui soutiendront notre approche centrée sur la décarbonisation, les nouvelles technologies et la transformation énergétique.

Heureusement pour nous, nous sommes tous différents. La diversité est notre moteur. Il fonctionne à l’inclusion, et notre énergie créatrice combinée est alimentée par plus de 130 nationalités. Siemens Energy célèbre la personnalité de chacun – quels que soient son origine ethnique, son genre, son âge, sa religion, son identité ou son handicap. Nous donnons de l’énergie à la société, à toute la société, et nous ne discriminons pas sur la base de nos différences.

Position Summary

The Dougherty lab (http://genetics.wustl.edu/jdlab/) is a mixed wet-lab dry lab environment studying gene expression in the brain in the context of psychiatric genetics. We are generating extensive transcriptomic (bulk RNA-seq, single cell RNA-seq, MPRA RNA-seq) datasets and need a creative, motivated and intelligent researcher to take the lead in the analysis and interpretation of this data. We have an extremely strong record in gene expression profiling analysis and can offer mentoring in the analysis of genomics experiments and the use of computational statistics.

Lirio is a technology/software company that provides expertise in a variety of behavioral science domains (e.g., behavioral economics, social psychology, public health), data science, and machine learning to drive consumer engagement, close gaps in preventive and chronic care, and promote health and well-being across an individual’s lifespan. Lirio’s behavior change AI platform unites behavioral science with advanced artificial intelligence (AI) to deliver Precision Nudging health interventions. Precision Nudging is the application of behavioral science to health interventions personalized by AI to each individual that overcome barriers to action at the right time and place for scalable, behavior change.

This is a remote role with the opportunity to be hybrid if located in Tennessee. All applicants must be authorized to work in the US without sponsorship.

To ensure an excellent onboarding experience and integration into the company, new colleagues will spend their first week onsite at one of our offices in Tennessee. Travel expenses will be paid. This is a requirement.

Position Summary

The Client Project Manager is responsible for planning, coordinating, and managing client implementations and related delivery work in accordance with established PMO standards. This role provides structured project leadership across scope management, schedule management, change control, launch readiness, and operational handoff. The Project Manager partners with client stakeholders and internal teams to define requirements, manage dependencies, track risks and issues, facilitate decisions, escalate barriers as appropriate, and maintain accurate project documentation. The ideal candidate brings strong project management discipline, client-facing communication skills, technical fluency, healthcare or SaaS implementation experience, and the ability to drive work forward through clear ownership and accountability.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Manage Scope, Plans, and Delivery Execution

Build and maintain project plans that define scope, milestones, workstreams, dependencies, owners, timelines, and acceptance criteria from kickoff through launch.
Manage scope in alignment with approved requirements, success criteria, timelines, and resource assumptions; identify potential scope changes and route them through the appropriate change control process.
Maintain accurate project documentation including project plans, status reports, decision logs, issue trackers, risk registers, and delivery artifacts required by PMO standards.
Provide regular visibility into project health including progress against milestones, open decisions, risks, issues, dependencies, and required leadership support.

Lead Governance, Change Control, and Escalation

Facilitate project governance routines including status meetings, stakeholder reviews, decision forums, risk reviews, and readiness checkpoints.
Apply change control discipline by documenting proposed changes, assessing impact to scope, schedule, cost, resources, quality, and client commitments, and coordinating approval before execution.
Use appropriate drive resolution of or use escalation authority to raise risks, unresolved decisions, resource constraints, timeline impacts, or delivery blockers to PMO leadership and accountable business owners.
Ensure decisions, approvals, assumptions, and tradeoffs are documented and communicated to affected stakeholders in a timely and consistent manner.

Coordinate Requirements, Resources, And Launch Readiness

Partner with clients and internal subject matter experts to gather, clarify, and document business, solution design, technical, and operational requirements.
Coordinate resource planning and competing priorities across internal teams by identifying required roles, timing, dependencies, constraints, and capacity needs to support project execution.
Manage launch readiness activities, including readiness criteria, testing support, defect or issue triage, operational preparation, client approvals, and go/no-go inputs.
Support transition from implementation to operations by coordinating handoff materials, support expectations, open items, ownership changes, and post-launch monitoring needs.

jobs.description:
Required Qualifications (as Evidenced By An Attached Resume)

Bachelor's degree (foreign equivalent or higher). In lieu of the degree, four (4) years of full-time directly related experience, or a combination of higher education and experience totaling four (4) years may be considered . Five (5) years of full-time, progressively responsible, directly related experience in construction management, budgeting, project development, and/or a related field. Supervisory experience in minor rehabilitation and new construction, including project cost and schedule oversight. Knowledge of Building and Fire Codes. Experience working with construction management software (Procore, E-Builder, Primavera, etc.). Project Management experience. Must have, keep and maintain the appropriate valid NYS Driver’s License; have a motor vehicle record which is free from major violations or a pattern of repeat violations. (***Out-of-State Applicants, see "Special Notes”).

Preferred Qualifications

Professional license (PE, RA) or professional certification (PMP, PgMP, CAPM, CEM, BSI, or CEO). Experience with minor rehabilitation and new construction in a University, Healthcare, Hospital Construction, or similar setting. OSHA certification. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and/or Google Workspace.

Brief Description Of Duties

The Project Manager will provide professional direction and oversight for all new construction and renovation activity. This includes responsibility for all duties necessary for project planning, such as identifying required labor and labor hours, calculating cost estimates based on trade rates/hours, working with trade unions in workforce designations, and ultimately managing and supervising assigned trades and contract labor and services for minor rehab and new construction services. The Project Manager will represent the University in development, planning, and construction activities performed in-house, utilizing state trade employees, contract labor, and consultants. The incumbent must be able to work independently while effectively managing multiple priorities and complex projects. They should demonstrate a strong track record of delivering construction and service projects that support cost-effective outcomes and maintain high-quality standards as well as have experience in interpreting and implementing design and construction documents. The purpose of the HSC Project Manager role is to ensure that both Capital and locally funded projects progress efficiently and on schedule. The selected candidate will be responsible for the following duties:

Manage multiple concurrent capital construction projects from scope through closeout.
Supervise vendors and trade personnel, including oversight of all trades in all facets of project progression, State trade employees, contract labor and outside vendors for work on major rehabilitations, renovations, alterations, and new construction projects.
Maintains all Capital Project documentation for adjustments to time, labor, extensions, and project scope change orders.
Maintain records of construction documents, as-built drawings, project schedules, using project management software, and budget estimates.
Provide accurate reports that forecast through project completion through the Project Status Report and other means identified by leadership.
Generate estimates and track time and materials to ensure projects are accomplished within time constraints and performance goals.
Order all construction material and equipment necessary for all capital projects through the procurement department on a project-by-project basis.
Review time sheets for union trades people, determine crew size requirements, and arrange for additional staff when needed.
Develop and manage construction project schedules, cost analysis, and project accounting in order to maintain project time tables for completion.
Construct projects by means of specifications, plans, scope of work, and cost estimates. This shall be conducted independently with little or no supervision.
Provide assistance to design engineers and architectural/engineering consultants for hands-on project management in construction.
Assist in the implementation of designs to conform to the budget and project scope.
Assist in developing requests for proposals (RFPs) and requests for qualifications (RFQs).
Inspect all construction plans and work from start to completion to verify conformity with the budget and project scope.
Review all construction plans and work from start to completion to verify conformance with New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code and Life Safety Code.
Other duties or projects as assigned, as appropriate to rank and departmental mission.

Special Notes

This is a full-time appointment. FLSA Exempt position, not eligible for the overtime provisions of the FLSA. Minimum salary threshold must be met to maintain FLSA exemption.

In addition to the employee's base salary, this position is eligible for $4,000 UUP annual location pay, paid biweekly.

Essential Position:
This has been designated as an essential position based on the duties of the job and the functions performed. Positions that are designated as such may be required to report to work/remain at work even if classes are canceled, and the campus is working on limited operations in an emergency.

Out-of-State Applicants: Please note as a condition of employment and in order for this position to be tendered, the successful incumbent will be required to provide evidence of a valid license and driving abstract from the state issuing the license within five business days of a conditional offer and must obtain a NYS driver's license within 30 days of start date.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Business Operations
jobs.description:
Established in 1993, Gadge USA is a national packaging supply and supply-chain solutions company with an expansive distribution network. We manage packaging portfolios across multiple categories through a scalable service model that delivers packaging solutions and continuous improvement to our customers.

The Project Manager - Business Operations
manages cross-functional projects and recurring business processes that support accurate execution, operational efficiency, and continuous improvement. This role brings structure and accountability to work involving Customer Accounts, Purchasing, Accounting, Finance, Projects, Sales, and other teams.

A key responsibility is managing the end-to-end vendor and customer price change process, including changes driven by index movements, contractual adjustments, and other business needs. When price change activity is lighter, this individual will manage additional operational projects and process improvement initiatives.

The successful candidate will organize work, coordinate stakeholders, validate data, manage communications, and drive initiatives from planning through implementation and follow-up. We are looking for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, proactive, and persistent in getting work completed.

A formal Project Manager title is not required.
Candidates may have developed these skills through business operations, executive support, project coordination, supply chain, finance, or other roles involving complex work and multiple stakeholders.

What You Will Do:

Project Management and Cross-Functional Coordination

Manage cross-functional projects from initiation through completion.
Define project scope, timelines, milestones, responsibilities, and action plans with stakeholders.
Coordinate activities across departments and ensure participants understand their deliverables and deadlines.
Monitor progress, anticipate delays, and proactively address roadblocks.
Follow up consistently and drive completion of agreed-upon actions.
Maintain project trackers and provide clear status updates to stakeholders and management.
Escalate unresolved issues and recommend practical solutions.
Confirm implementation is complete and review results to identify gaps and lessons learned.

Price Change Management

Own and coordinate the complete vendor and customer price change process.
Monitor relevant pricing publications and track contractual requirements, effective dates, and required approvals.
Partner with Purchasing, Finance, Customer Accounts, Sales, and other teams to validate calculations, supporting data, and pricing impacts.
Coordinate the preparation and issuance of vendor and customer notifications.
Ensure communications accurately reflect approved adjustments, effective dates, supporting documentation, and contractual requirements.
Work with stakeholders to address questions, exceptions, and customer or vendor concerns.
Coordinate required system updates and verify that changes are implemented accurately and on time.
Maintain complete records supporting price changes and conduct post-implementation reviews.

Data Management and Reporting

Review project data, calculations, and documentation for accuracy and completeness.
Use Excel to analyze information, reconcile discrepancies, and develop tracking and reporting tools.
Work with stakeholders to resolve data inconsistencies before implementation.
Maintain organized records of approvals, communications, decisions, and implementation activities.
Keep relevant customer, contract, and pricing information aligned across Salesforce, the ERP, and SharePoint.

Operational Projects and Process Improvement

Manage additional operational projects based on business priorities and available capacity.
Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, improve coordination, and reduce errors.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, checklists, and workflow documentation.
Support the implementation of tools and processes that improve visibility and accountability.
Work with department leaders to turn improvement opportunities into practical action plans.
Incorporate lessons learned into future projects and recurring processes.

Requirements

Required Skills and Experience:

3-5+ years of experience coordinating complex initiatives, managing operational processes, or supporting cross-functional projects. Relevant backgrounds may include business operations, executive support, project coordination, supply chain, or finance.
Demonstrated ability to take ownership of work, manage timelines, and coordinate multiple stakeholders to drive completion.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
Ability to anticipate problems, address gaps, and follow up effectively without relying on constant direction.
Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including data analysis, pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and tracking and reporting tools.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently and influence others without direct authority.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience managing operational projects, recurring business processes, or process improvement initiatives.
Experience working with customer or vendor data, contracts, pricing, or cost changes.
Familiarity with ERP systems, such as Sage/MAS 100.
Experience with Salesforce and SharePoint.
Experience developing SOPs, checklists, and workflow documentation.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Supply Chain, Operations, or a related field.
Prior pricing experience and a formal project management background are helpful but are not required. We welcome candidates—including experienced executive assistants and operations professionals—who can demonstrate that they have successfully organized complex work, exercised sound judgment, and driven initiatives through completion.

The Ideal Candidate Will Be:

An organized professional who brings structure to complex work.
Proactive and persistent in moving initiatives forward.
Comfortable working with detailed data and checking accuracy.
A clear communicator who builds productive relationships across departments.
Accountable for results and willing to address issues directly.
Process-minded, with the ability to identify improvements and follow through on implementation.
Adaptable as priorities shift between recurring processes and new projects.

Benefits

What We Offer:

A competitive salary, including annual discretionary cash bonus.
Your health is important! We offer excellent healthcare (medical, dental, vision) benefits with national providers, short-term and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, employee assistance program, and mental health support programs such as Talkspace and Sondermind
We provide paid time off including company paid holidays

The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

About The Role

Position Is Contingent Upon Award**

Peraton Labs is hiring an Information System Security Manager (ISSM) to be the single point of contact to Covered California and the accountable owner of oversight, timely execution, and quality for every security service Peraton delivers to the California health benefit exchange and the CalHEERS eligibility and enrollment system. You will lead a small, senior, multi-disciplinary security team spanning governance and compliance, security architecture and engineering, incident response, third-party risk, technical security, monitoring, and data protection.

You will work directly with Covered California's CISO and Information Security Officer, technical and project teams, business stakeholders, and independent assessors. The goal is to keep a system that carries the personal, health, and financial information of millions of Californians measurably secure, continuously compliant with NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, ARC-AMPE, and IRS Publication 1075, and ready for CMS Authority to Connect review.

What You Will Do In This Role:

Lead the security team. Manage and coordinate the day-to-day activities of assigned information security personnel; provide leadership, mentoring, and direction, and own deliverable accuracy, consistency, and schedule adherence across all seven contracted service areas.
Serve as the primary client security liaison. Act as the single operational point of contact among contractor personnel, Covered California security leadership, technical teams, project teams, and business stakeholders, and deliver regular status, risk, and escalation reporting to security leadership.
Own the compliance and GRC engine. Manage security activities tied to NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls; coordinate development and review of security policies, procedures, standards, and plans; direct GRC activities and platforms; and maintain the risk register.
Drive risk down to closure. Oversee risk assessments, control reviews, gap analyses, and remediation; track weaknesses, findings, and Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms) through verified closure.
Serve as backup incident manager. Support the incident response program in coordination with the client Information Security Officer, and coordinate investigations, evidence handling, communications, escalation, reporting, and post-incident review; participate in the on-call incident response rotation.
Coordinate technical and third-party security work. Guide security architecture and engineering reviews across cloud and on-premises environments and technical security work spanning network, endpoint, vulnerability management, identity and access management, cloud, and application security; manage vendor security due diligence, assessments, contract and control reviews, and monitoring.
Coordinate assessment and penetration testing logistics while preserving assessor independence. Provide evidence, scheduling, and remediation ownership for the annual independent assessment and penetration test cycle without directing or influencing the independent assessors' scope, judgments, or findings.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information systems, information technology, or engineering. In lieu of a degree, an equivalent combination of education, professional certification, and additional relevant experience will be considered.
12+ years of progressively responsible cybersecurity experience, including managing security programs, teams, or major security workstreams. (Note: eight years is the absolute floor for equivalency consideration; the posted target is 12+.)
Active CISSP or CISM certification.
Demonstrated experience managing security activities against the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control set in a complex enterprise environment.
Demonstrated experience owning a risk register and managing POA&Ms, findings, and corrective action plans through closure, using an enterprise GRC platform or comparable control-tracking system.
Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor senior technical personnel while working collaboratively with client stakeholders, and to brief cybersecurity risk credibly to both technical and executive audiences in writing and in person.
US Citizenship and the abillity to pass a California criminal background clearance (Gov. Code
1043 / 10 CCR
6456) before starting work or accessing any confidential information, PII, PHI, federal tax information, or financial information.

Desired:

Master's degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information systems, or a related discipline.
PMP certification. CGRC, CRISC, or CCSP are also valued.
Hands-on experience with ARC-AMPE (ACA, Medicaid and Partner Entities) security and privacy requirements.
Experience with IRS Publication 1075 compliance and federal tax information (FTI) control management.
Experience with CMS cybersecurity requirements and the CMS Authority to Connect (ATC) process or comparable federal authorization processes.

Muon seeks a Senior Technical Program Manager - Propulsion Systems to lead the end-to-end planning of the development, manufacturing and test of our propulsion systems.

This role may be worked remotely from an approved location.

Responsibilities

Mastering program schedules: You will own the full propulsion program roadmap. That means staying ahead of the curve across development, testing, parts procurement, and assembly, then mapping all of that into an active production flow while knowing exactly when hardware is "good enough" to move forward.
Bridging products and programs: You will serve as the primary link to our product group, helping guide strategic product decisions and making sure the overall roadmap gets executed without a hitch.
Driving thruster production: You will keep supply chains steady and kitting organized, track timeline needs for specific spacecraft missions, cut through organizational friction to keep production moving, and decide on pragmatic timing for introducing product upgrades.
Maintaining clear team communication: You will keep dialogue flowing across engineering leads, managers, and executives to minimize unexpected surprises or crossed wires.
Managing customer relationships: You will act as the point person for our thruster customers—understanding their pain points, sharing transparent updates, knowing when discretion is needed, and involving the broader propulsion engineering team only when required.
Translating needs into test priorities: You will break down top-level mission specs into clear testing targets, pinpointing exactly what must be proven on the test stand and building realistic plans to validate it.
Integrating across hardware teams: You will ensure propulsion works hand-in-hand with the rest of hardware—leveraging our machine shop, tapping mechanical engineering expertise, and coordinating sensible electrical integration efforts.
Advocating for the big picture: You will keep an eye on industry trends, competitor moves, and market shifts to help make tough choices that drive Muon's overall success.

5+ years working in engineering or program management environments.
A relevant degree in engineering, physical sciences, or a related technical field.

Job Description

At Norton Rose Fulbright, people thrive because of a shared commitment to quality, unity and integrity. The highly regarded law firm consistently receives recognition from Great Place to Work and Top Workplaces, two companies that specialize in assessing organizational culture. Teams collaborate across regions, value new ideas and deliver meaningful client solutions, supported by a culture that embraces ambition, development and shared success. With more than 3,000 lawyers and 3,000 business services professionals working together across 50 offices worldwide, this global law firm provides a full range of legal services to leading corporations and financial institutions operating in key markets and sectors.

As an early adopter of advanced eDiscovery technology and methodologies, the Firm's Global eDiscovery Services Department provides strategic services to our disputes lawyers and clients. Working alongside other talented professionals, you'll be surrounded by an open and collaborative culture that embraces recognition and professional development.

The Sr. Project Manager, eDiscovery Cyber Services leads eDiscovery and data analysis workstreams for complex cyber incident response (CIR) matters, from initial data assessment through review, extraction, normalization, entity resolution, notification and reporting. Partnering with the firm's Cybersecurity practice, clients, forensic providers, review providers and other third parties, the role manages scope, cost, risk, quality and delivery while developing defensible, efficient strategies that make effective use of technology.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Lead eDiscovery and data analysis strategies for complex CIR matters, including file listing analysis, data assessment, identification of sensitive data, defensible reduction, review, extraction, normalization, entity resolution, notification and reporting.
Serve as the senior eDiscovery/CIR advisor and primary point of contact for assigned matters, translating technical and data issues into practical strategies, risks, options and recommendations for legal teams, clients and stakeholders.
Design, validate and document defensible methodologies for data reduction, identification of sensitive data, search term calibration, statistical sampling, analytics and other technology assisted workflows.
Coordinate with forensic providers, clients, legal teams, vendors and review teams on secure data assessment, transfer, workflow design, quality control, productivity, budgets, timelines and deliverables.
Develop and manage matter budgets, forecasts, work plans, resource needs, metrics and customized reporting; monitor scope, costs and vendor spend and proactively identify variances.
Oversee extraction, normalization, entity resolution, deduplication, address validation and development of notification lists, including analysis of anomalies, near duplicates and matching issues using SQL, advanced Excel, scripts, queries or other data transformation techniques as appropriate.
Support legal teams and clients in interpreting data findings, methodologies, metrics, notification populations and responses to client or regulatory inquiries.
Serve as an escalation point for complex project, technology and vendor issues while maintaining active ownership of complex matters and delegating effectively.

Leadership and professional development

Mentor and develop Project Managers, Project Analysts and other team members through coaching, knowledge sharing and guidance on active matters.
Help shape the department’s Cyber eDiscovery service model, standards, playbooks and process improvement initiatives.
Evaluate emerging technologies and analytics approaches that may improve quality, efficiency, defensibility or client outcomes.
Expand consulting, client service and leadership capabilities through increasingly complex matters and initiatives that span multiple practice and business functions.

Other duties

Please note this job description does not cover or contain all activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

This position is remote and can therefore be located in any city where we have a US office. Flexibility to visit the office for training or meetings is required.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree required.
Minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in eDiscovery, litigation support, legal technology or related consulting, including significant project management responsibility, and at least one year managing or substantially leading matters involving cyber incident response, data breaches or sensitive data review.
Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex matters with large data volumes; advise attorneys, clients and senior stakeholders on strategy, workflow, risk, cost and technology; and lead multidisciplinary teams, outside providers and escalations.
Advanced Excel skills required, including XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, Power Query and Power Pivot/DAX; experience analyzing, formatting and reporting on large structured and semistructured datasets.
Minimum of three years of Relativity experience, with advanced proficiency in review workflows, analytics and reporting; Relativity Certified Administrator certification preferred but not required.
Experience with complex structured and unstructured data, including millions of documents or rows of information, sensitive data elements and privacy classifications such as PII and PHI, as well as personal data subject to GDPR.
Ability to manage multiple projects under rigorous deadlines with limited direction, exercise sound judgment, follow established procedures and remain flexible to support urgent matters outside standard business hours, including early mornings, evenings and occasional weekends.
Preferred but not required: experience with database tools such as MS SQL, Access or Oracle; scripting or automation using Python, PowerShell or APIs; advanced analytics, machine learning, AI review tools or other emerging technologies; and visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues clearly to legal teams, clients and nontechnical stakeholders.

The Program Manager brings structure and visibility to complex initiatives, manages timelines and dependencies, identifies risks and blockers, and facilitates effective communication across teams. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Product Management, Operations, Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
3–5 years of experience in program management, project management, product operations, product management, or a related field.
Experience working in a technology, software, or other product-driven environment.

Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Ability to influence and coordinate stakeholders without direct authority.

Preferred

Organization: Creates structure, maintains accurate documentation, and effectively manages competing priorities.
Collaboration: Builds productive relationships across Product and partner functions.
Communication: Clearly communicates status, risks, decisions, and next steps.

Facilitate working sessions, planning meetings, status meetings, and project reviews.
Build alignment across teams with shared goals and interdependent deliverables.

This is a hybrid position.

At Children’s, the region’s only full-service pediatric healthcare center, our people make us the very best for kids. Come cultivate your passion, purpose and professional development in an environment of excellence and inclusion, where team members are supported and deeply valued. Opportunities for career growth abound as we grow our services and spaces, including the cutting-edge Hubbard Center for Children. Join our highly engaged, caring team—and join us in providing brighter, healthier tomorrows for the children we serve.

Children's is committed to diversity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer including veterans and people with disabilities.

A Brief Overview

Project Manager independently leads the delivery of moderate-complexity healthcare IT, clinical, and business initiatives, applying industry best practices to drive successful outcomes. This role is accountable for end-to-end project delivery, including collaborative planning and accountability for scope, schedule, budget, quality, resources, communication, risk, and stakeholder engagement. Project Manager develops and manages integrated project plans, ensuring alignment with organizational goals related to patient care, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and strategic priorities. This role manages multiple projects concurrently and is responsible for delivering projects on time, within scope, and within budget. Working cross-functionally, the Project Manager leads project teams and influences stakeholders, including clinical leaders, operational partners, IT teams, vendors, and external partners. The role serves as the primary point of accountability for project performance and proactively addresses risks, issues, and dependencies. This position provides clear, timely, and actionable reporting to leadership and stakeholders, supporting informed decision-making and optimizing communication. Additionally, the Project Manager may provide guidance to operational teams and contribute to multi-workstream initiatives within a Strategic Project Management Office (SPMO) environment. Overall, this role demonstrates increasing independence, ownership, and accountability while delivering measurable project outcomes and contributing to organizational success.

Essential Functions

Project Leadership, Integration & Delivery
Independently leads moderate-complexity projects through initiation, planning, execution, monitoring & controlling, and closing while remaining in alignment with industry’s best practices
Develop integrated project plans that align scope, schedule, cost, resources, risks, and communications.
Establish and maintain project governance structures, decision frameworks, and escalation paths.
Makes and supports shared decisions on project delivery, mitigations, and priorities.
Manage multiple projects concurrently.
Ensure alignment between project deliverables, organizational strategy, and healthcare operational priorities.

Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Build and maintain strong partnerships with multidisciplinary teams, including IT, clinical, operational, and business leaders.
Serve as a trusted liaison between Ancillary teams, IT teams, and operational stakeholders to support planning, implementation, and ongoing operational readiness.
Coordinate with resource managers to secure and manage project resources across multiple departments and affiliated organizations.
Facilitate effective project meetings, workshops, and decision‑making forums, while ensuring strong collaboration.
Facilitate and provide opportunities for consensus building among project owners and engaged stakeholders, fostering alignment, accountability, and shared ownership of outcomes.
Provide leadership to project teams by setting expectations, promoting transparency, and encouraging constructive feedback and collaboration.
Develop and execute communication plans tailored to diverse healthcare audiences.

Prioritization, Time Management & Adaptability
Demonstrate the ability to prioritize tasks, manage time, and be adaptable
Partner with departmental leadership to assess, prioritize, and balance project workloads based on organizational strategy and capacity.
Successfully manage multiple projects concurrently in dynamic environments with competing priorities and evolving constraints.
Delegate tasks appropriately, set clear expectations, and monitor progress to ensure accountability and delivery.
Demonstrate flexibility and sound judgment when responding to shifting priorities, risks, and organizational needs.
Provide project advisory support to operational leaders and contribute to broader portfolio initiatives within the Strategic Project Management Office (SPMO).
Perform additional duties in support of the Strategic Project Management Office as required.

Technology & Methodology Expertise
Apply and continuously enhance knowledge of project management methodologies, tools, and best practices (e.g., waterfall, agile, hybrid, PMBOK framework).
Maintain working knowledge of relevant domains such as Information Technology, clinical systems, business process improvement, and healthcare operations, with an ability to accommodate adult learning modalities.
Leverage project and portfolio management tools to track progress, manage dependencies, and report outcomes effectively.
Manage projects involving clinical applications, cross‑department initiatives involving EHRs, interfaces, and vendors, healthcare infrastructure, and business systems.
Active participation in outage coordination and impact management, even when not the formal outage owner.
Ensure project planning accounts for patient safety, clinical workflows, data integrity, and system interoperability.
Support operational readiness ownership, including training, cutover, and transition to support.
Support operational readiness activities, including go-live planning, workflow validation, training, and transition to support in collaboration with leadership and clinical experts.
Partner and collaborate with different internal stakeholders, to maintain awareness of healthcare regulatory considerations such as HIPAA, data privacy, and audit requirements.

Project Administration, Reporting & Tool Proficiency
Coordinate internal and external resources, working with functional leaders and vendors to secure appropriate expertise.
Monitor vendor performance, deliverables, and contractual commitments.
Facilitate collaboration across multidisciplinary and geographically distributed teams.
Maintain comprehensive project documentation including charters, plans, schedules, risk logs, and status reports.
Create and manage project plans within the project management tool (e.g., Planview).
Develop workflow and process maps (using Visio, Power Point, Word) to support clinical and operational clarity.
Establish and manage project workspaces and documentation repositories (e.g., SharePoint).
Produce standard and executive‑level reporting to support decision‑making and oversight.
Coordinate meetings, prepare agendas, document decisions, and distribute meeting minutes.

Education Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university (e.g. Information Technology, Business, Organizational Communication, Healthcare Administration, Public Health, Project Management, Construction Management, or a related healthcare or business discipline (e.g., Nursing [RN], Medical Technology, Pharmacy, etc.). Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered. Advanced degrees are advantageous. Required or
Equivalent work experience may be substituted for education Required

Experience Qualifications

Minimum 3 years’ experience in information technology, strategic planning, health care operations, project management or other relevant professional experience Required or
Minimum 3 years’ experience in project management Required

Skills And Abilities

Ability to develop, lead, and facilitate project requests, planning activities and teams comprised of executive leadership, operational leaders, and clinical staff.
Ability to utilize critical thinking skills.
Skill in use of MS Office and Project Management tools.
Highly effective organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple, complex initiatives concurrently in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Demonstrated adaptability and flexibility to meet deadlines, navigate ambiguity, and lead through change.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with team members, leaders, executive leadership, and external partners in a wide variety of settings
Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with a collaborative approach to influencing and aligning diverse stakeholders.
Ability to think strategically
Knowledge of and/or ability to learn and operate computer software programs; spreadsheet (Excel); graphics (PowerPoint); word-processing (Word); and project management tools and software (PPM Pro) and Project Management Systems.
Willingness to escalates issues/concerns to appropriate level of management.
knowledgeable of applying technology to Healthcare.
Strong organization, analysis and problem-solving skills are required with an emphasis on attention to detail and the ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously.

Licenses and Certifications

Make Your Impact At a Leading Fintech Company

Led by the office of the General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer, BILL's Legal and Compliance function supports the company's growth and governance and builds trust with its customers, partners and regulators.

BILL is looking for a tech-savvy Sr. Privacy Program Manager to help scale privacy operations across the Legal and Compliance team. This person will own key parts of BILL's privacy program and work closely with Product, Engineering, Information Security, CX and Procurement.

The Sr. Privacy Program Manager reports to the Director, Legal and helps set and carry out BILL's privacy strategy. They will own privacy impact assessments, data subject requests and vendor privacy reviews. They will also look for ways to make the program more efficient, including through smart use of automation and AI tools.

What You Will Do

Own and scale core parts of BILL's privacy and data governance program.
Serve as the primary point of contact for privacy escalations, data subject requests, and privacy questions from across the company.
Own the DSAR program end to end, including intake, tracking, fulfillment, metrics and process improvements in partnership with CX.
Lead privacy impact assessments for new products, features and vendors that process personal data.
Run privacy reviews for AI features and internal AI tool adoption, working with Legal, InfoSec and Product.
Build and maintain data maps and records of processing, and stay current on company systems that hold personal data.
Develop and deliver privacy training for employees and specific teams.
Draft and maintain privacy policies, procedures and standard operating procedures.
Monitor changes to privacy laws and regulations (CCPA/CPRA, US state privacy laws, GDPR and emerging AI rules) and explain what they mean for the business.
Find and roll out automation and AI tools that make privacy operations more efficient and scalable.
Track and report privacy program metrics to Legal leadership.

What You Bring

7+ years of experience in privacy, compliance or technology program management, including at least 4 to 5 years focused on privacy program operations (DSARs, PIAs/DPIAs, TIAs, ROPAs, vendor privacy reviews, cookie consent management, etc). Experience at a software, fintech or payments company preferred.
Working knowledge of CCPA/CPRA, US state privacy laws, GLBA, GDPR, HIPAA.
Hands-on experience using AI tools (such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, GC.ai or Harvey) in daily work, for example to draft documents, summarize regulations, review contracts, or speed up assessments and request workflows. Candidates should be ready to share specific examples.
Familiarity with privacy risks tied to AI, such as training data use, model inputs and outputs, and vendor AI terms, and experience assessing them.
Experience with privacy tech platforms (such as OneTrust, Transcend or TrustArc).
Ability to work with all levels of management, multiple geographies, subject matter experts, legal staff, vendors and customers.
Ability to pull together information from many sources and present it clearly and concisely.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Self-starter who spots issues and opportunities early and recommends actions.
Strong prioritization, organization and follow-through in a fast-paced environment.
Works well as part of a team.
Bachelor's degree.
CIPP/US, CIPP/E, CIPM or CIPT certification preferred. JD a plus, not required.

Responsibilities

The Senior Project Manager (PM) works independently, assuming primary responsibility for planning, directing, coordinating, and delivering project activities through the entire project life cycle (from initiation through handoff to customer) that are major, complex, and business critical. The Senior PM is responsible for leading project objectives and completion on time, on budget, and in conformance with Mayo Clinic project management methodologies and standards.

The Senior Project Manager serves as the portfolio execution leader for Pharmacy Intelligence & Automation. This role is responsible for coordinating and driving strategic initiatives involving pharmacy analytics, automation, artificial intelligence (AI), reporting, operational transformation, and technology optimization across Mayo Clinic pharmacy practice.

The position provides program leadership for a growing portfolio of initiatives and supports enterprise-wide deployment of innovative solutions that improve medication safety, operational efficiency, workforce productivity, regulatory compliance, and financial stewardship. The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to manage a complex portfolio of strategic initiatives, work effectively with executive leaders and frontline staff, establish governance processes, translate strategy into execution, develop roadmaps and executive-level communications, track value realization and return on investment, lead organizational change efforts, and coordinate analytics, automation, AI, and innovation initiatives across pharmacy.

In addition to managing complex individual projects, this role provides oversight and coordination for an enterprise portfolio of strategic initiatives, ensuring work is appropriately prioritized, governed, resourced, measured, and successfully adopted.

The Senior PM will lead large projects that have site- or enterprise-level strategic importance. Project work has high to very high risk and risk interdependencies, multiple interrelationships, and may have major costs associated. Responsible for managing established budgets, the Senior PM leads and provides direction in the development and tracking of project budgets. The position requires strict adherence to budget management practices and guidelines of both the assigned department and the institution.

The Senior PM independently leads problem-solving and decision-making activities within the scope of the project and change management process, taking reasonable and prudent actions to accomplish agreed-upon project objectives. This individual leverages extensive experience to manage large-scale initiatives and is highly competent in the implementation and sustainment of project outcomes. Advanced negotiation skills, strategic thinking, and innovative problem-solving are essential to this role.

In addition to traditional project management responsibilities, this role is expected to support portfolio governance, strategic planning, executive reporting, stakeholder engagement, organizational change management, resource coordination, and benefits realization activities for enterprise pharmacy initiatives.

The use and application of Agile, Lean, and continuous improvement methodologies is important to this role. The successful candidate must be comfortable leading both technology-focused and operational transformation initiatives while adapting project approaches to meet organizational needs.

Guiding teams on Agile practices and values to implement critical projects.
Assessing team and organizational maturity and coaching teams to higher levels of performance and effectiveness.
Removing impediments and blockers or guiding teams to do so; escalating appropriately when necessary.
Building a trusting and collaborative environment where issues can be openly raised and resolved.
Facilitating completion of work without coercion, assignment, or directive management approaches.
Facilitating discussion, decision making, and conflict resolution.
Supporting and educating Product Owners, particularly regarding backlog development and backlog refinement.

May have direct and indirect reports and may be responsible for leading and developing project staff in a goal-oriented manner. The Senior Project Manager leads and demonstrates a project-focused culture at Mayo Clinic and serves as a mentor and advisor to others regarding project management practices, methods, and standards.

This role will frequently interact with executive leaders, pharmacy operational leaders, informatics professionals, analysts, technology teams, and clinical stakeholders. Success requires strong executive communication skills, strategic thinking, influence without authority, and the ability to translate organizational priorities into executable plans while managing multiple concurrent initiatives.

Automation and workflow optimization initiatives.
AI and advanced analytics programs.
